entities.title: Core Themes & Tone
entities.summary: Avalymia explores a universe steeped in complex themes, including the weight of history, the clash of cultures, and the profound nature of existence.
entities.contentMd: Avalymia explores a universe steeped in complex themes, including the weight of history, the clash of cultures, and the profound nature of existence. At its core is cosmic horror, which manifests not just in monstrous forms, but in an indifferent or malevolent universe revealed through its layered structure, unpredictable temporal flows, and enigmatic, powerful entities like the Archdemons. A central narrative driver is the consequence of power, starkly illustrated by the dangers of forbidden knowledge, the irreversible psychological breakdown or corruption resulting from altered states like Demonification or Awakening, and the perilous side effects of manipulating reality through magi-tech or dividing one's essence through soul fragmentation. The overall tone balances elements of grand high fantasy, with its diverse planes, races, and divine lore, with a prevailing grimdark atmosphere marked by existential dread, deep suffering, and pervasive moral ambiguity.

entities.title: Avalymia
entities.subtitle: Also known as Universe, Multiverse
entities.summary: The Universe of Avalymia is a great expanse encompassing all that exists.
entities.contentMd:
The Universe of Avalymia is a great expanse encompassing all that exists. 
# Structure of The Universe

![avalymia structure](/vaults/avalymia/images/avalymia-structure.webp)

Though a continuous space, it is commonly conceptually divided into three layers, each has its own properties, and containing an unknowable number of Planes of Existence.
## Layers

1. The [[Void]]
2. The [[Avalymian Cloud]]
3. The [[Convergence Well]]

entities.title: Avalymian Cloud
entities.summary: This layer represents the middle of the universe, where the laws of physics and magic are quite normal and there aren't many anomalies.
entities.contentMd: This layer represents the middle of the universe, where the laws of physics and magic are quite normal and there aren't many anomalies. Worlds in the Avalymian Cloud are considered stable in terms of time flow and magical fields.

entities.title: Convergence Well
entities.summary: This layer of the universe is located on its innermost level. The worlds in this layer are so dense that the borders between them seem to fade.
entities.contentMd:
This layer of the universe is located on its innermost level. The worlds in this layer are so dense that the borders between them seem to fade. Additionally, time in this layer flows infinitely slower relative to the outer layers.

The [[Nexus]] lies at the center of this layer.

entities.title: Void
entities.summary: The outermost layer of the universe is an endless expanse of near vacuum where magic cycles so slowly as to be practically dormant, and time accelerates to an unimaginable tempo.
entities.contentMd:
The outermost layer of the universe is an endless expanse of near vacuum where magic cycles so slowly as to be practically dormant, and time accelerates to an unimaginable tempo. Worlds perceived within the Void are separated by vast gulfs of nothingness, their forms faint and unfinished.

Though it was once believed that worlds originate in the Void, modern cosmological consensus rejects this notion. The Void lacks the magical density required for planar genesis. Instead, its extreme temporal acceleration creates a profound distortion:

the early future-states of forming planes refract outward and become visible in the Void long before their physical stabilization occurs in the Avalymian Cloud.

To an external observer, a world seems to “appear” in the Void, drifting inward over ages toward the Cloud. In truth, this is merely the Void’s temporal lens revealing a plane’s distant timeline ahead of schedule. The world itself coalesces deeper within the universe, only later collapsing inward as its temporal field stabilizes.

This phenomenon—once deemed a cosmic impossibility—is now understood as a natural consequence of the universe’s layered time-flow. Worlds do not come from the Void; they are only seen there first, as echoes cast ahead of their own formation.

entities.title: Nexus
entities.subtitle: Also known as The Crucible
entities.summary: At the center of Avalymia lies "The Nexus," also referred to as "The Crucible". a world that attracts and absorbs all other worlds.
entities.contentMd: At the center of Avalymia lies "The Nexus," also referred to as "The Crucible". a [[Plane of Existence|world]] that attracts and absorbs all other worlds. All other planes of existence revolve around the Nexus and slowly draw closer to it until they merge with it.

entities.title: Plane of Existence
entities.subtitle: Also known as World, Realm, Plane
entities.summary: "Plane of Existence", otherwise known as “World” or “Realm”, refers to a distinct reality that exists within the universe.
entities.contentMd: "Plane of Existence", otherwise known as “World” or “Realm”, refers to a distinct reality that exists within the universe. Each Plane of Existence is unique and may have its own physical laws, inhabitants, and characteristics.

entities.title: World Shard
entities.subtitle: Also known as World Fragment
entities.summary: A World Shard is a solitary fragment of a Plane of Existence that has been severed from its original reality.
entities.contentMd:
A World Shard is a solitary fragment of a [[Plane of Existence]] that has been severed from its original reality. Existing in a unique state of being, these shards drift through the cosmic expanse of the Avalymian universe, carrying with them the remnants of civilizations, geography, and history from their lost home.

World Shards are born from cataclysmic events that shatter the fabric of a world. Shards can be created during violent collisions between planes, where fragments are torn away and flung outward into the universe.

The merging of a World Shard is an act of cosmic displacement, as the fragment descends, it forces the existing terrain downward into the depths, seamlessly grafting its own alien landscape onto the surface of the receiving world in its place.

entities.title: Conduits
entities.subtitle: Also known as Conduit
entities.summary: Conduits are mysterious objects scattered throughout the realm, imbued with an intense concentration of magical energy.
entities.contentMd:
Conduits are mysterious objects scattered throughout the realm, imbued with an intense concentration of magical energy. When spells are cast in their vicinity, the potency and accuracy of the magic is amplified, though the consequences of misjudging their power can be dire indeed, resulting in anything from physical exhaustion to death itself.

Conduits emit their own localized resonance fields that add to the universal field, increasing effective frequency in their vicinity. This also explains their temporal effects—areas near powerful Conduits experience both enhanced magic AND [[time dilation]].

# Field Distortion
Field Distortion occurs when Conduits or Foundation Stones emit their own localized resonance, interfering with the Universal Resonance Field. These distortions create pockets of altered time and enhanced magic that can dramatically affect their immediate surroundings.

The most famous example is the [[Chronogem]], a Foundation Stone capable of creating severe temporal anomalies. In its presence, the effective pulse frequency can increase by orders of magnitude, causing time to flow at vastly different rates within meters of each other. Scholars working near powerful Conduits have reported completing years of research in what their colleagues experienced as days.

entities.title: Foundation Stones
entities.subtitle: Also known as Foundation Stone
entities.summary: Foundation Stones are Conduits of immense magical influence that can shape the fabric of reality.
entities.contentMd: Foundation Stones are [[Conduits]] of immense magical influence that can shape the fabric of reality.

entities.title: Magic System
entities.subtitle: Also known as Magic
entities.summary: In the world of Avalymia, magic is an enigmatic force that permeates every aspect of existence.
entities.contentMd: In the world of [[Avalymia]], magic is an enigmatic force that permeates every aspect of existence. Its power is highly dependent on a myriad of factors, including the proximity of the caster to certain [[Conduits]], as well as the proximity of the plane of existence to the [[Nexus]].

entities.title: Abyssal Compression
entities.summary: Abyssal Compression is the movement of The Lithic Song focused on the manipulation of mass and pressure. It is the most physically destructive application of Menti magic.
entities.contentMd:
**Abyssal Compression** is the movement of **[[The Lithic Song]]** focused on the manipulation of mass and pressure. It is the most physically destructive application of [[Menti]] magic.
## Mechanics
By vibrating their shell at a specific, low-frequency pitch, a Menti can cause the surrounding water molecules to contract or expand violently. 
- **The Pressure-Well:** A Menti can localize the crushing pressure of the deepest trenches onto a single point—such as a diver's lung or a ship's hull—without affecting the surrounding water.
- **Buoyancy Erasure:** By disrupting the density of the water directly beneath a vessel, the Menti can cause it to lose all buoyancy, pulling it into the depths as if it were made of solid lead.
## Atmospheric Impact
In the dark, crushing silence of the Eastern Spine, the use of Abyssal Compression is felt before it is seen. Sailors describe it as a "sudden tightening of the chest" and the sound of wood "screaming" before the hull implodes.

entities.title: Conduit Tapping
entities.summary: Conduit Tapping is the art of drawing magical power directly from Conduits—particularly Foundation Stones, the most potent magical objects in existence.
entities.contentMd:
Conduit Tapping is the art of drawing magical power directly from [[Conduits]]—particularly [[Foundation Stones]], the most potent magical objects in existence. While all magic benefits from proximity to these artifacts, Conduit Tapping involves establishing a direct channel between practitioner and stone, allowing raw magical energy to flow into the caster. The results are spectacular: vastly amplified spellcasting, abilities that would otherwise be impossible, power that rivals divine intervention. The costs are equally dramatic.

The [[Golyzmia]], the pale star-farers who dig beneath their mountain fortresses, appear to have mastered a form of Conduit Tapping that powers their technology and possibly their starships. The black smoke billowing from their settlements may be a byproduct of this process.

entities.title: Divine Tongue
entities.summary: Divine Tongue is the purest and most powerful form of magic known to exist—the language of creation itself.
entities.contentMd:
Divine Tongue is the purest and most powerful form of magic known to exist—the language of creation itself. It is believed to be the speech used by [[Avalama]] when first bringing the cosmos into being and later employed by the [[Trinity of Gods]] to shape the [[Plane of Existence|planes of existence]]. Unlike other magical disciplines that manipulate existing forces, Divine Tongue speaks reality into existence. Words uttered in Divine Tongue do not describe what is; they define what shall be.

Divine Tongue operates on the fundamental principle that each word carries the weight of primordial creation, resonating with the underlying structure of reality. The language cannot be learned through conventional study; it must be remembered, as though recalling something the soul has always known. Some theorize that all sapient beings carry fragments of Divine Tongue buried deep within their essence—echoes of Avalama's original utterance that gave rise to consciousness itself.

The ancient [[Adyni]] were the only civilization known to have achieved systematic mastery of Divine Tongue. When the Adyni vanished, this knowledge was largely lost. What fragments remain exist in scattered ruins, half-understood inscriptions, and the occasional prodigy who spontaneously manifests a word or two—usually with catastrophic results.

Divine Tongue is extraordinarily dangerous precisely because of its power. A mispronounced word does not fail—it succeeds at creating something wrong.

entities.title: Echo-Siphoning
entities.summary: Echo-Siphoning is the most sacred and guarded movement of The Lithic Song. It is a form of ancestral necromancy that allows a Menti to commune with the "Echoes" left behind in the Ossuary Reefs.
entities.contentMd:
# Echo-Siphoning

**Echo-Siphoning** is the most sacred and guarded movement of **[[The Lithic Song]]**. It is a form of ancestral necromancy that allows a [[Menti]] to commune with the "Echoes" left behind in the **[[Ossuary Reefs]]**.

## The Residual Soul
In the Avalymian universe, an object etched with a life's history gains **[[Ontological Weight]]**. When a Menti dies, their shell retains a harmonic imprint of their consciousness and the unique spells they mastered.
- **Siphoning the Echo:** By wrapping their body around an ancestral shell and vibrating at a matching frequency, a living Menti can "retrieve" knowledge. This is a slow, meditative process that feels like a shared dream between the living and the dead.
- **The Echo-Guards:** The collective vibration of an Ossuary Reef acts as a natural defense system, projecting waves of disorientation and "Soul-Ache" to any non-Menti who approaches with hostile intent.

## The Taboo of Erasure
To "siphon" a shell too aggressively can destabilize the residual soul, leading to **Ontological Erasure**. This is considered the ultimate desecration of a Menti's legacy.

entities.title: Fleshcraft
entities.summary: Fleshcraft is the direct magical manipulation of living tissue—reshaping bodies, accelerating healing, altering physical form, and blurring the boundaries between one organism and another.
entities.contentMd:
Fleshcraft is the direct magical manipulation of living tissue—reshaping bodies, accelerating healing, altering physical form, and blurring the boundaries between one organism and another. It is among the most powerful and most controversial of magical disciplines, celebrated by some as the highest expression of healing arts and condemned by others as blasphemous tampering with creation. The truth, as with most magic, depends entirely on the practitioner's intentions.

At its most benign, Fleshcraft accelerates natural healing, closes wounds, and repairs damaged organs. More advanced applications include reshaping bone structure, grafting tissue between organisms, and inducing controlled mutations. The most skilled practitioners can rebuild bodies from catastrophic injury, restore lost limbs, or even alter fundamental characteristics like height, coloration, and facial structure. Some historical accounts—disputed but persistent—claim the [[Adyni]] used Fleshcraft to create [[Elf|Elves]] from [[Human|human]] stock, deliberately engineering a subspecies with enhanced magical aptitude and extended lifespan.

Fleshcraft raises profound questions about the relationship between body and soul. If a practitioner gradually replaces every part of a person's body, is the result still the same person? Religious authorities across multiple traditions have issued condemnations, arguing that the body is a sacred vessel not meant for arbitrary modification. Others counter that healing has always involved changing the body—Fleshcraft merely extends the healer's reach. The debate remains unresolved.

The line between Fleshcraft and the early stages of [[Awakening]] or [[Demonic Corruption (Condition)]] remains disturbingly unclear. Both conditions involve uncontrolled transformation of living tissue; some scholars theorize they may be Fleshcraft without a practitioner—the body reshaping itself according to external influences. More immediate dangers include rejection (flesh that refuses the intended change), cascade mutation (changes that spread beyond the target area), and psychological trauma from experiencing one's body as malleable rather than fixed. Several documented cases describe practitioners who could no longer stop modifying themselves, compulsively reshaping their forms until nothing recognizable remained.

entities.title: Green Tongue
entities.summary: Green Tongue is an ancient form of primal magic enabling communication between sapient beings and the living world—animals, plants, fungi, and virtually any organism possessing life force.
entities.contentMd:
Green Tongue is an ancient form of primal magic enabling communication between sapient beings and the living world—animals, plants, fungi, and virtually any organism possessing life force. Green Tongue functions as a bridge of understanding, translating intent and emotion across the gulf separating different forms of consciousness.

Green Tongue is not a language in the conventional sense—it possesses no grammar or vocabulary that can be transcribed. Rather, it functions as empathic resonance amplified through magical channels. When a speaker addresses a living creature, they project meaning through vocalization, emotional intent, and subtle magical emanation that bypasses species-specific limitations. The receiver perceives this in whatever manner is natural to their consciousness.

Communication clarity varies based on the creature's cognitive complexity, magical proximity to Conduits or the Nexus, and the speaker's familiarity with the species. Crucially, Green Tongue conveys meaning—it does not compel obedience. A hungry predator understands a plea perfectly well; it simply may not care. The ability cannot reach non-living matter, undead whose life force has been severed.

[[Elf|Elves]] show the highest natural affinity among human derivatives, while [[Emeshar Tal]] possess the ability as naturally as breathing. The magic finds use in agriculture (negotiating with crops for better yields), wilderness navigation (asking local fauna about water sources or dangers), healing (communicating with living tissue to encourage recovery), and espionage (every mouse in a castle wall becomes a potential witness). Extended use carries psychological risks; practitioners may experience identity erosion or difficulty distinguishing their thoughts from those of creatures they've communed with.

entities.title: The Lithic Song
entities.summary: The Lithic Song is the ancestral and primary magic system of the Menti. It is a discipline of harmonic resonance, where the practitioner's stone shell acts as a focus and amplifier for the raw currents of the Universal…
entities.contentMd:
# The Lithic Song

**The Lithic Song** is the ancestral and primary magic system of the **[[Menti]]**. It is a discipline of harmonic resonance, where the practitioner's stone shell acts as a focus and amplifier for the raw currents of the **[[Universal Resonance Field]]**.

## Foundations
Unlike the visual or spoken magics of surface races, the Song is entirely tactile and rhythmic.
- **Somatic Resonance:** Menti cast by vibrating their translucent flesh against the unique runes etched inside their **Lithic Carapace**. 
- **The Amplification Spiral:** The spiral shape of the shell is designed by nature and modified by art to create a perfect acoustic chamber, allowing a Menti to project magical intent through miles of water.

## Disciplines of the Song
The Lithic Song is traditionally divided into three distinct "Movements":

1.  **[[Abyssal Compression]]**: The manipulation of hydrostatic pressure and the physical "weight" of the ocean.
2.  **[[Viscous Weaving]]**: The infusion of slime with mana to create detection lattices and tangible structures.
3.  **[[Echo-Siphoning]]**: The extraction of residual memories and spells from the shells of the deceased.

entities.title: Viscous Weaving
entities.summary: Viscous Weaving is the movement of The Lithic Song that focuses on sensory extension and construction. It utilizes the Menti's iridescent, highly conductive mucus as a medium for magical intent.
entities.contentMd:
**Viscous Weaving** is the movement of **[[The Lithic Song]]** that focuses on sensory extension and construction. It utilizes the Menti's iridescent, highly conductive mucus as a medium for magical intent.

## The Resonance-Silk
Menti infuse their slime with specific mana-frequencies to create **Resonance-Silk**, a substance that is nearly invisible underwater but highly sensitive to vibration.
- **Lattice Casting:** Menti "weave" massive, submerged webs across reef entrances. Any movement within the web is instantly transmitted to the Menti's sensory tendrils, granting them a form of localized omniscience.
- **Structural Mucus:** Through rhythmic vibration, a Menti can harden their silk into semi-solid structures, allowing them to mend coral, trap prey, or seal off chambers within the reef.

## Communication
While [[Menti]] do not "speak" in the human sense, they can use Viscous Weaving to transmit complex chemical and vibrational messages through the silk, allowing for near-instant communication across a connected reef-web.

entities.title: Magical Intensity
entities.summary: Magical intensity is influenced by multiple factors:
entities.contentMd:
Magical intensity is influenced by multiple factors:
1. **Proximity to other [[Plane of Existence|planes of existence]]**: All planes of existence emit a magical field that governs the intensity of magic. mutual influences between overlapping fields can intensify magic in the vicinity.
2. **[[Conduits]] / [[Foundation Stones]]**: mysterious objects that either emit magical fields themselves or amplify fields around them.
3. **Proximity to the [[Nexus]]**: Though other planes of existence influence magical intensity as well; The Nexus emits a magical field of immense magnitude.

entities.title: Universal Resonance Field
entities.subtitle: Also known as Magic Field, Magical Field, Temporal Field
entities.summary: The Universal Resonance Field is the fundamental metaphysical substrate underlying all magical and temporal phenomena in Avalymia.
entities.contentMd:
The Universal Resonance Field is the fundamental metaphysical substrate underlying all magical and temporal phenomena in [[Avalymia]]. It manifests as a cyclic pulse of energy that permeates every [[Plane of Existence|plane of existence]], governing both the intensity of magical forces and the relative flow of time.

The field operates through regular cycles, each beginning with a detectable energy surge known as a Nexus Pulse. The frequency of these pulses—the time between them—varies dramatically based on proximity to the center of the universe. Near the [[Nexus]], pulses occur with extraordinary rapidity; in the Void, the interval between pulses stretches to incomprehensible lengths.

This variation in pulse frequency directly correlates with two observable phenomena: [[Magical Intensity|magical intensity]] and temporal dilation. Where pulses are frequent, magic flows with tremendous potency and time passes slowly relative to outer regions. Where pulses are rare, magic lies dormant and time races forward.

The origin of the Universal Resonance Field remains a subject of intense theological and scientific debate. Some believe the field was initiated during [[El Adoniah Detalash Roni]]—the Contraction of [[Avalama]]—when the primordial consciousness withdrew to create space for existence. Others maintain that the field is a natural property of the cosmos, no more requiring explanation than the existence of space itself. What is certain is that before the field began its pulse, time as we understand it did not exist, and events from that primordial era cannot be placed on any conventional timeline.

# Nexus Pulse
A Nexus Pulse is the detectable energy surge that marks the beginning of each cycle in the Universal Resonance Field. These pulses emanate from the center of [[Avalymia]] and propagate outward through all planes of existence, though their frequency varies dramatically based on location.

On [[Ezob]], at the heart of the [[Nexus]], pulses occur with extraordinary regularity—approximately once per local day under normal conditions. In the [[Avalymian Cloud]], the period between pulses extends to weeks, months, or years depending on distance from the center. In the [[Void]], where magic sleeps and time races, pulses may be separated by what would constitute millennia in Nexus time.

The detection and counting of Nexus Pulses forms the foundation of advanced timekeeping throughout Avalymia. Scholars and mages have developed specialized instruments capable of perceiving these subtle energy signatures. By counting pulses and calculating temporal ratios between locations, travelers can determine how much time has passed in one plane relative to another.

The pulse also serves as an anchor for magical workings. Many advanced rituals require synchronization with the pulse cycle, and spells cast at the exact moment of a pulse are said to carry additional potency. Certain rare conditions—such as pulse confluence, when local distortions align with the universal pulse—can create windows of extraordinary magical potential.

entities.title: Shared Dreamscapes
entities.summary: Within Avalymia, consciousness is not always an isolated phenomenon. Under specific conditions—often involving potent psychoactive substances, deep meditative states, targeted magic, strong psychic resonance, or…
entities.contentMd:
Within [[Avalymia]], consciousness is not always an isolated phenomenon. Under specific conditions—often involving potent psychoactive substances, deep meditative states, targeted magic, strong psychic resonance, or proximity to certain planar conjunctions or [[Conduits|conduits]]—multiple minds can become temporarily interlinked. This creates a Shared Dreamscape, a temporary, subjective reality constructed from the overlapping subconscious landscapes of the participants.

These convergences are not mere shared hallucinations; they possess a tangible, albeit non-physical, structure where thoughts, memories, fears, and desires can manifest with startling vividness, sometimes perceived or even interacted with by all participants. The stability and coherence of a Shared Dreamscape vary wildly, often influenced by the number of participants, their mental discipline, the method of induction, and any guiding influence present.

While spontaneous occurrences are exceedingly rare and often chaotic, induced Shared Dreamscapes can potentially be used for deep communication, psychological exploration, shared learning, or even conflict resolution, as the raw truths of the subconscious are laid bare. However, navigating these spaces is perilous, risking psychic feedback, mental fragmentation, or becoming lost within the collective subconscious.

Scholarly terms include Oneiric Convergence or Collective Psychic Resonance Fields. The [[Niran|Nirani]] civilization's mastery and ritualization of this phenomenon, utilizing the [[Dreamcap]] mushroom and guided by [[Tzanarim]], represent the most sophisticated known application, known as the Dream Trials.

entities.title: Dementia
entities.summary: Some souls do not depart cleanly at death—they unravel while life persists. Dementia is a gradual dissolution of the soul while the body continues to function, often spanning years or decades.
entities.contentMd:
Some souls do not depart cleanly at death—they unravel while life persists. Dementia is a gradual dissolution of the soul while the body continues to function, often spanning years or decades. Memories go first—a beloved face becomes unfamiliar, cherished skills vanish overnight, names of children and parents slip away. Then personality erodes, passions cease to matter, the warm heart grows cold. Finally, emotions themselves fade—joy, sorrow, love becoming distant concepts remembered intellectually but no longer felt.

The horror lies in awareness. Sufferers watch themselves disappear piece by piece, mourning each fragment of identity as it slips away, knowing eventually they will no longer remember they were ever anyone at all.

entities.title: Soul-Bleed
entities.summary: Echoes are emotional imprints left after death—recordings of intense feeling that persist in locations, objects, or people.
entities.contentMd:
Echoes are emotional imprints left after death—recordings of intense feeling that persist in locations, objects, or people. But when such an Echo imprints upon a living soul, the result is Soul-Bleed: two identities occupying the same space, boundaries dissolving until neither knows where one ends and the other begins. This is not possession—it is something more insidious.

Early symptoms are subtle: weeping at a stranger's face, speaking phrases in unknown languages, profound nostalgia for unvisited places. As it progresses, the afflicted may answer to the [[Echo]]'s name, pursue the Echo's unfulfilled goals, love those the Echo loved. They might look in a mirror and feel the face staring back is wrong—that they should be someone else entirely.

entities.title: Soullessness
entities.subtitle: Also known as Hollow, Husk
entities.summary: When the soul is torn away by force, the body normally dies. But sometimes, rarely, it does not.
entities.contentMd:
When the soul is torn away by force, the body normally dies. But sometimes, rarely, it does not.

When the soul is severed, the body does not die, and the mind does not vanish. Instead, the individual (Hollow) enters a state of absolute inertia. To the observer, a Hollow appears indistinguishable from one consumed by profound apathy. They may remain motionless for hours, ignoring hunger, thirst, or danger, not because they are physically unable to move, but because the internal drive to initiate action has been excised.

Contrary to the belief that they are "empty," the Hollow remains fully conscious. They possess memory, logic, and sensory awareness. They feel the pain of starvation and the shame of their condition. They may scream internally, commanding their body to rise, but the mechanism that translates intent into action is gone. They are prisoners in their own flesh, forced to observe their slow decay with agonizing clarity.

The Open Door A Hollow offers no resistance to spiritual intrusion. Without a Will to claim the body’s space, they are porous vessels for Wandering Souls or Demons. Many Hollows do not merely succumb to possession but tacitly invite it. In the crushing silence of their paralysis, even the malicious drive of a hostile entity is preferable to the stillness. They surrender the reins simply to remember the sensation of movement

entities.title: Temporal Displacement
entities.summary: Normally, body and soul exist in the same temporal frame. But this unity can fracture, leaving the soul operating on a different frequency than the flesh it inhabits.
entities.contentMd:
Normally, body and soul exist in the same temporal frame. But this unity can fracture, leaving the soul operating on a different frequency than the flesh it inhabits. The effects are often subtle enough to be mistaken for personality traits.

When the soul runs faster than the body, the afflicted appear unnaturally quick—reacting before events fully occur, finishing others' sentences, moving with unsettling precision. They seem perpetually impatient, anxious, as though everyone around them moves through honey. Such individuals often excel at tasks requiring rapid thought but struggle with patience and contemplation.

When the soul runs slower than the body, they appear dreamy, detached, perpetually lost in thought. They respond to questions asked minutes ago, seem incapable of quick decisions, and drift through conversations as though half-asleep. Others often assume diminished intelligence, though the truth is far stranger.

The rarest and most disorienting form—the Scattered—are souls unmoored from linear time entirely. They experience past, present, and future simultaneously: answering questions before they're asked, mourning friends still living, greeting strangers with the warmth of long friendship because that friendship has already formed. Most appear mad. Perhaps they are.

entities.title: Tethered
entities.summary: Some souls become bound to one another so intensely that death cannot separate them. When one Tethered dies, their soul remains anchored by the living partner—a Wandering Soul bound not to place but to person.
entities.contentMd:
Some souls become bound to one another so intensely that death cannot separate them. When one Tethered dies, their soul remains anchored by the living partner—a [[Wandering Soul]] bound not to place but to person. The survivor is followed always by the presence of their dead beloved, unable to fully interact yet never entirely absent. They cannot find peace in grief, for grief implies absence. Many go mad. Others take their own lives, hoping to reunite—but this does not solve the problem.

When both Tethered are dead, neither can move on—each anchors the other to existence. They become a composite entity, two identities merged into one tormented presence, speaking with two voices, pursuing conflicting goals, loving and resenting each other throughout eternity.

entities.title: Demonic Corruption
entities.subtitle: Also known as Demonification
entities.summary: Unlike calculated Lichdom, Demonic Corruption (also known as Demonification) is tragedy—unwilling transformation through exposure to Derdama.
entities.contentMd: Unlike calculated Lichdom, Demonic Corruption (also known as Demonification) is tragedy—unwilling transformation through exposure to [[Derdama]]. Early stages are subtle: disturbing visions, intensifying negative emotions, eroding moral boundaries. Then physical changes manifest—features twisting, limbs multiplying, flesh taking unnatural hues. Finally, the original personality is obliterated entirely, replaced by a being of suffering and the compulsion to create more. The most powerful become [[Archdemon|Archdemons]], shaping entire regions of Derdama according to their nature.

entities.title: Lichdom
entities.summary: Lichdom requires separating one's soul from one's body and housing it in a phylactery—an external vessel. The body becomes animated by will rather than life, decaying but never failing.
entities.contentMd:
Lichdom requires separating one's soul from one's body and housing it in a phylactery—an external vessel. The body becomes animated by will rather than life, decaying but never failing. The soul can reanimate it even after destruction, so long as the phylactery remains intact. Some liches divide their soul across multiple phylacteries, creating networks of anchors—but consciousness stretched too thin may fragment, the original identity dissolving into competing voices.

This immortality devastates. The process warps the soul, eroding empathy until only obsession remains. Most liches retreat from society entirely, pursuing incomprehensible goals or simply waiting for purposes long forgotten.

entities.title: Undeath
entities.summary: Undeath forces the dead into semblance of life through necromancy, demonic influence, or divine curse. Unlike the Chaining, the undead move and act—but the soul is not free.
entities.contentMd: Undeath forces the dead into semblance of life through [[Fleshcraft|necromancy]], demonic influence, or divine curse. Unlike the [[Chaining]], the undead move and act—but the soul is not free. For souls within, undeath is slavery: bound to decaying flesh, forced to animate it, unable to move on to whatever fate awaited them. Many undead are driven by desperate hunger for release.

entities.title: Chaining
entities.summary: The Chaining occurs when the body dies but the soul fails to depart—remaining tethered to its former vessel, conscious and aware but unable to animate the corpse or free itself.
entities.contentMd:
The Chaining occurs when the body dies but the soul fails to depart—remaining tethered to its former vessel, conscious and aware but unable to animate the corpse or free itself. The soul perceives everything: the coldness of dead flesh, the slow corruption of decay, the voices of mourners. Yet it cannot speak, move, or signal its presence. It is imprisonment in the most intimate cell imaginable—one's own corpse.
# The Horror of Animation
The Chaining becomes more terrible when the corpse begins to move again. Through necromancy or demonic influence, the body may reanimate while the chained soul remains a helpless passenger. It watches through eyes it cannot direct as rotting hands strike flesh, as teeth tear into those it loved—screaming silently for any death that might free it from this puppetry.

Even when the body finally collapses into rot, the soul often remains anchored—aware but immobile—until all remains are destroyed. This fate has made destruction of the recently dead a sacred duty in many cultures.
# Religious Exploitation
Certain faiths teach that only the faithful can be guaranteed proper release upon death. The unfaithful risk eternal imprisonment in rotting flesh. These doctrines create powerful incentives for compliance—the faithful pay for rituals ensuring their soul's departure. Whether these rituals work or merely exploit fear remains debated. More troubling are accounts of religious authorities deliberately inducing the Chaining in heretics as punishment.

entities.title: Echo
entities.summary: Distinct from souls, Echoes are emotional imprints—recordings of intense feeling stamped onto locations or objects. They have no consciousness, merely playing back fragments when triggered.
entities.contentMd: Distinct from souls, Echoes are emotional imprints—recordings of intense feeling stamped onto locations or objects. They have no consciousness, merely playing back fragments when triggered. Most are subtle: faint feelings, fleeting images glimpsed from the corner of one's eye. Potent Echoes manifest with startling clarity, often mistaken for true hauntings. They persist only as long as emotional anchors remain strong, fading as memories weaken.

entities.title: Wandering Soul
entities.summary: When a chained soul's body is destroyed, release does not guarantee True Death. Many emerge still bound to the mortal realm—Wandering Souls, present but unable to fully interact.
entities.contentMd: When a [[Chaining|chained]] soul's body is destroyed, release does not guarantee True Death. Many emerge still bound to the mortal realm—Wandering Souls, present but unable to fully interact. Some retain coherence, haunting familiar places, attempting communication through dreams. Others fade into twilight existence, drifting on metaphysical currents. Still others become consumed by the emotions that anchored them, transforming over time into stable forms: Guardian Spirits protecting what they loved, Vengeful Ghosts seeking justice or harm, or rarely, Higher Spiritual Entities that transcend their mortal nature entirely.

entities.title: Natural Life
entities.summary: Natural life is characterized by the harmonious union of body and soul, each sustaining the other. The body ages, heals, hungers, and eventually fails; the soul animates, perceives, remembers, and feels.
entities.contentMd: Natural life is characterized by the harmonious union of body and soul, each sustaining the other. The body ages, heals, hungers, and eventually fails; the soul animates, perceives, remembers, and feels. Body and soul are tethered—a bond so fundamental that severing it typically destroys both. When the soul departs, the body dies. When the body fails beyond recovery, the soul is released. This is the natural order, though disease, violence, or misfortune can thrust the unprepared into liminal spaces where neither state fully claims them.

entities.title: Preserved Immortality
entities.summary: Not all who live forever do so through corruption. Preserved Immortality extends natural life without fundamentally altering the relationship between body and soul—typically achieved through divine favor, powerful…
entities.contentMd:
Not all who live forever do so through corruption. Preserved Immortality extends natural life without fundamentally altering the relationship between body and soul—typically achieved through divine favor, powerful artifacts, or proximity to certain [[Conduits]]. The Preserved Immortal does not age past a certain point but remains capable of death through violence or catastrophic injury. Crucially, they retain full capacity for emotion, growth, and change, distinguishing them from those who achieve endless existence through darker means.

Such beings often become figures of legend: undying sages watching civilizations rise and fall, eternal guardians protecting sacred sites across millennia. Whether their immortality is blessing, or burden depends on temperament—and how many loved ones they watch grow old while they remain unchanged.

entities.title: Awakened Reincarnation
entities.summary: A form of reincarnation where the reborn retains full memories of previous lives—born already ancient in infant bodies.
entities.contentMd: A form of reincarnation where the reborn retains full memories of previous lives—born already ancient in infant bodies.

entities.title: Cyclical Reincarnation
entities.summary: A form of reincarnation where the soul is trapped in loops, reliving the same life until some condition is met.
entities.contentMd: A form of reincarnation where the soul is trapped in loops, reliving the same life until some condition is met.

entities.title: Reincarnation
entities.summary: Reincarnation returns the soul to mortal existence in new form. Most commonly, souls are reborn without memories—experiencing only unexplained affinities: skills that come easily, places that feel familiar, people to…
entities.contentMd:
Reincarnation returns the soul to mortal existence in new form. Most commonly, souls are reborn without memories—experiencing only unexplained affinities: skills that come easily, places that feel familiar, people to whom they are inexplicably drawn.

Directed Reincarnation places souls deliberately into specific bodies by divine intervention. Forced Reincarnation—soul slavery—inserts souls into bodies against their will.

entities.title: Soul Mark
entities.summary: Some individuals bear Soul Marks: birthmarks echoing past wounds, innate abilities from previous lives, metaphysical signatures visible to those with the sight.
entities.contentMd: Some individuals bear **Soul Marks**: birthmarks echoing past wounds, innate abilities from previous lives, metaphysical signatures visible to those with the sight. Bearers often attract attention from those who knew their former incarnations—inheriting debts, duties, or enemies they never chose.

entities.title: States of Persistence
entities.summary: Throughout the Avalymian multiverse, existence is not binary. One does not simply live or die—there exists a spectrum of states between vibrant life and absolute annihilation.
entities.contentMd:
> "In Avalymia, death is not a door but a corridor—and not all who enter find their way to the end."
> — Inscription on the gates of ash, author unknown
# The Spectrum of Being
Throughout the [[Avalymia|Avalymian]] multiverse, existence is not binary. One does not simply live or die—there exists a spectrum of states between vibrant life and absolute annihilation. While these intermediate conditions can manifest anywhere in the universe, they grow increasingly common near the [[Nexus]], where dense magical fields and overlapping planar boundaries disrupt the natural processes of mortality.

On [[Ezob]] itself, dying naturally cannot be taken for granted. The cessation of breath does not guarantee the departure of the soul. The stillness of the heart does not promise rest. Understanding these states shapes everything from religious practice to burial customs, from medical treatment to legal systems.

## Part I: The Living States
1. [[Natural Life]]
2. [[Preserved Immortality]]
## Part II: Afflictions of the Living
Not all horrors wait until death to claim their victims. Certain conditions afflict the living, eroding the bond between body and soul while life persists.
1. [[Dementia]]
2. [[Soullessness]]
3. [[Soul-Bleed]]
4. [[Tethered]]
5. [[Temporal Displacement]]
## Part III: True Death
1. [[True Death]]
2. [[Afterlife]]

## Part IV: The Intermediate States
Between the warmth of life and the finality of True Death lie intermediate states—conditions where dying has been interrupted, corrupted, or subverted.
1. The [[Chaining]]
2. [[Wandering Soul]]
3. [[Echo]]
## Part V: Corrupted Immortality
1. [[Lichdom]]
2. [[Demonic Corruption]]
3. [[Undeath]]
## Part VI: Total Annihilation
1. [[Soul Death]]
2. [[Soul Consumption]]
## Part VII: [[Reincarnation]]
1. [[Awakened Reincarnation]]
2. [[Cyclical Reincarnation]]
3. [[Soul Mark|Soul Marks]]

entities.title: Soul Consumption
entities.summary: Soul consumption absorbs one soul into another—the dominant gaining access to memories, abilities, and magical essence.
entities.contentMd:
Soul consumption absorbs one soul into another—the dominant gaining access to memories, abilities, and magical essence. Masters of the practice have absorbed dozens or hundreds of souls, becoming entities of terrifying might.

But each absorbed soul leaves its mark. Personality bleeds through: habits, fears, desires from the consumed manifest in the consumer. The consumed rarely go quietly, creating internal conflict—voices, impulses, episodes of lost control. Some consumed souls persist as fragments, whispering from the margins, nudging behavior inexplicably. In severe cases, the consumer becomes a patchwork of everyone devoured, original self-drowning in fragmentary others. Some consumed souls accumulate enough coherence to attempt a coup—seizing control and relegating their former predator to passenger.

entities.title: Soul Death
entities.summary: Beyond True Death lies Soul Death: complete destruction of the soul itself. No afterlife, no lingering presence, no possibility of return. The individual is simply gone—erased as thoroughly as if they never existed.
entities.contentMd:
Beyond True Death lies Soul Death: complete destruction of the soul itself. No afterlife, no lingering presence, no possibility of return. The individual is simply gone—erased as thoroughly as if they never existed. This can occur through soul consumption by another entity, magical cataclysm, or abilities that strike the soul directly.

Most cultures view Soul Death with horror—the worst possible fate. Yet for those trapped in endless suffering—liches without purpose, undead bound to rotting flesh, demons remembering dimly what they once were—it represents ultimate release. Small cults venerate oblivion, seeking total annihilation. For those who have suffered beyond bearing, the promise of true ending holds undeniable appeal.

entities.title: Afterlife
entities.summary: The nature of the afterlife remains a matter of faith. Among followers of the Adyni creation myth, righteous souls join the Tasvani in the plane of Rogim, while the wicked face judgment.
entities.contentMd:
The nature of the afterlife remains a matter of faith. Among followers of the [[Adyni]] creation myth, righteous souls join the [[Tasvani]] in the plane of [[Rogim]], while the wicked face judgment. The [[Niran|Nirani]] hold a cyclical view—souls return to the Deep, the primordial darkness from which their ancestors emerged, resting until called forth again by the [[Hollow Flame]].

Regardless of specific beliefs, the afterlife shapes society profoundly. The promise of reward or punishment beyond death influences moral behavior, provides comfort to the grieving, and gives meaning to mortal struggle. Spiritual leaders hold enormous influence, their pronouncements carrying weight in everything from personal ethics to political decisions.

entities.title: True Death
entities.summary: In a universe with countless fates worse than death, True Death is actively sought.
entities.contentMd: In a universe with countless fates worse than death, True Death is actively sought. It is the complete cessation of bodily function followed by clean separation of soul from flesh, allowing departure for whatever afterlife awaits—death as it should be. The soul departs the mortal realm entirely. What lies beyond remains a matter of faith, for no soul that achieved True Death has returned to report.

entities.title: Ezob Local Calendar
entities.summary: While the Nexus Pulse System serves as the universal standard for interplanar coordination, the inhabitants of Ezob primarily use a local calendar based on the arrival of humanity to their world.
entities.contentMd:
While the [[Timekeeping|Nexus Pulse System]] serves as the universal standard for interplanar coordination, the inhabitants of [[Ezob]] primarily use a local calendar based on the arrival of humanity to their world. This system, known as the **Era of Man (EM)**, predates the NPS by millennia and remains the dominant civil calendar across [[Human|human]], [[Niran]], and most mixed settlements on Ezob.
# Era Designations
## Era of Man (EM)
Years following the First Landing—the arrival of the first human world shards on Ezob—are counted in the **Era of Man**. Year 1 EM marks the establishment of the first permanent human settlement.
## Before Man (BM)
Events predating human arrival are designated **Before Man (BM)**. This era encompasses the age of the Emeshar, the flourishing of the Adyni, and all primordial history.
# The Year
The Ezobian year is a Lunisolar system, strictly governed by the phases of the moon [[Ru'una (Moon)|Ru'una]] and the solar seasons.

The Standard Year consists of 11 Months, each lasting exactly 30 days

To reconcile the 11 lunar months (**330 days**) with the solar year **(~360 days**), a 12th Month is added approximately every three years.

**The Nameless Month**: This 12th month has no name. It is represented in dates only by a blank space or a silent notation. It is commonly referred to as The Silent Month or The Hollow Month.
# The Months
The moon, Ru'una, is not merely a celestial body but a divine guardian created to protect Ezob from evil. The calendar is therefore a spiritual cycle of safety and vulnerability.
## The Vigil (Full Moon)
The nights of the Full Moon (Days 14–16) are considered the holiest and safest of the month.

**Blessing**: Ru'una’s influence is at its zenith. These days are favored for weddings, healing rituals, and major contracts.

**The Silver Nights**: Cities often hold festivals or night markets during this time, as the light of Ru'una is believed to suppress the influence of Derdama and weaken the power of Archdemons.

## The Blind Days (New Moon)
The final three days of every month (Days 28–30), when Ru'una vanishes from the sky.

**Fear**: The world is considered "unguarded." It is believed that the barrier between Ezob and the Underworld is thinnest during this dark window.

**Taboos**: These are days of caution. In many cultures, leaving one's home after dusk is forbidden, mirrors are covered, and no new endeavors are begun. To be born during the Blind Days is considered an ill omen.

## The Eleven Named Months

The standard months are named after the eleven known [[Sentiani]], the divine guardians of the world.

### Iyar
 Named for the Sentiani [[Iyar]]. 
 Marks the beginning of the year and the spring thaw.
### Jenjo
Month of Heat, Named for [[Jenjo]].
### Amon
Named for [[Amon]].
### Kez
Named for [[Kez Mish'ol]].
### Avar
Named for the Sentiani [[Avar]].
### Mozeta
Named for the Sentiani [[Mozeta]].
### Elher
Named for the Sentiani [[Elher]].
### Sebatonin
Named for the Sentiani [[Sebatonin]].
### Haas
Named for the Sentiani [[Haas]].
### Ticmary
Named for the Sentiani [[Ticmary]].

### Tevet
Month of Frost, Named for the Sentiani [[Tevet]].
This is the final named month, coinciding with deep winter.

### The Nameless Month 
Leap Month inserted after Tevet during leap years, this month corresponds to the Twelfth, [[Unknown Sentiani]].

**Nature**: It is a time "outside of time." Because it belongs to an erased god, the month is treated as a void in the calendar.

**Cultural Practice**: It is a month of stillness and debt. Courts are closed, and official decrees are suspended. It is traditional to settle old grievances during this time, so they do not carry over into the new year.

**Superstition**: Magic performed during the Nameless Month is considered unstable, and children born during this time are often called "The Unwritten," believed to possess destinies that cannot be predicted by seers.

entities.title: Time
entities.summary: The division of the universe into layers is necessary because time flows differently in each plane of existence.
entities.contentMd:
The division of the universe into [[Avalymia|layers]] is necessary because time flows differently in each plane of existence. This is influenced by factors such as the size of the world and its distance from the center of the Universe.

Temporal flow rate is directly affected by magical fields, the stronger the magical field, the slower time flows relatively.

Time in Avalymia flows according to the rhythm of the [[Universal Resonance Field]]. The [[Universal Resonance Field|pulse]] frequency experienced at any location determines both the local flow of time and the intensity of magical forces. Worlds near the Nexus experience rapid pulses—time flows slowly there, and magic burns bright. In the outer reaches, pulses are rare; time races forward, and magic sleeps.

As planes approach the [[Nexus]], their boundaries blur, a realm of chilling stillness where time stands frozen, and magic pulsates with raw intensity.

This innermost layer, where the convergence reaches its zenith, is the realm of the Nexus itself and the infinite worlds that orbit it closely.

entities.title: Timekeeping
entities.summary: The Nexus Pulse System (NPS) is the standardized universal timekeeping framework adopted by interplanar scholars, travelers, and institutions requiring coordination across planes of existence.
entities.contentMd:
# Nexus Pulse System
The Nexus Pulse System (NPS) is the standardized universal timekeeping framework adopted by interplanar scholars, travelers, and institutions requiring coordination across planes of existence. It is based on the counting of [[Universal Resonance Field|Nexus Pulses]] from a fixed reference point known as Pulse Zero

## Pulse Zero
**Pulse Zero (P0)** represents the epoch from which all NPS dating is calculated. Historical records suggest this corresponds to the establishment of the first interplanar pulse-counting network, centered on [[Ezob]]. Events after Pulse Zero are designated with the suffix PE (Pulse Era), while events before are marked PPE (Pre-Pulse Era). The system functions analogously to the Before/After distinction in local calendars.

The genius of the NPS lies in its universality. Because all planes experience the same pulses—albeit at different subjective frequencies—a pulse count provides an objective measure of cosmic time. A traveler departing Ezob at pulse 50,000 PE and arriving at a distant plane still at pulse 50,000 PE (from the universe's perspective) can calculate precisely how much local time has passed in each location by comparing pulse periods.

Most cultures maintain their own local calendars for daily use, based on planetary rotations, seasons, or cultural events. The NPS exists as a scholarly overlay, essential for historical coordination, interplanar commerce, and diplomatic treaties that span worlds with vastly different temporal flows.
# Resonance Decay
Resonance Decay refers to the gradual change in a [[Plane of Existence|plane's]] pulse period as it moves through the universe. As planes drift toward the [[Nexus]] over cosmic time, their pulse periods shorten—time slows relative to the outer regions, and magic intensifies. Conversely, [[World Shard|world shards]] moving outward experience lengthening pulse periods, accelerating time and diminishing magical potency.

For stable planes in the[[Avalymian Cloud]], this decay is imperceptibly slow, measured in fractions of change over thousands of years. However, for World Shards traversing unusual trajectories, the effect can be dramatic. A shard spiraling inward toward the [[Nexus]] might experience centuries of temporal compression, arriving at its destination with its inhabitants having aged mere years while millennia passed in the Cloud.

Some scholars have proposed that careful measurement of resonance decay rates across multiple planes could reveal the age of the [[Universal Resonance Field]] itself—and by extension, the moment of [[Avalama]]'s Contraction. This research remains controversial, as it touches on questions that many religious authorities consider matters of faith rather than calculation.

entities.title: El Adoniah Detalash Roni
entities.subtitle: Also known as Adyni Creation Myth
entities.summary: Creation myth originating from the ancient Adyni culture.
entities.contentMd:
Creation myth originating from the ancient Adyni culture.

El Adoniah Detalash Roni is the foundational creation myth of the ancient [[Adyni]] civilization. The narrative describes the origin of the cosmos through the self-diminishment of [[Avalama]], a primordial consciousness that contracted itself to create space for existence. To overcome loneliness, Avalama divided into the [[Trinity of Gods]]: [[Elom]] (the Dreamer), [[Tas'va]] (the Architect), and [[Rogim]] (the Witness).

Together, the Trinity filled the first plane ([[Asban]]) with stars and worlds, yet nothing they created possessed true life. Elom secretly created the world Ezob and upon it brought forth the Adyni—mortal beings with free will. Rogim discovered this secret and, moved by the beauty of mortal life, agreed to help conceal it.

When Tas'va discovered the betrayal, he exiled Elom to the [[Void]]. Consumed by guilt, Tas'va sacrificed his divinity to create the [[Tasvani]] (lesser gods) and the [[Sentiani]] (twelve guardians), then entered the Void to search for Elom.

As to what happened to Rogim, there are two contradicting stories:

One version says that Rogim descended to Ezob, and in sorrow, fell into slumber, waiting for their final reunion. The slumbering Rogim, is the fertile ground on which the first [[Emeshar]] emerged from.

The other version mentions the [[Nir]], 600 radiant descendants born from Rogim's ultimate sacrifice of divinity. Rogim, now both creator and guide, dwells among them, leading his children through realms shaped by his sorrow and wisdom. The Nir embody fragments of Rogim’s essence, each a living testament to the god’s enduring presence and selfless creation.

The myth establishes core Avalymian theological concepts: creation through sacrifice, divine imperfection, and the origin of mortality as a gift rather than curse. It explains why the original gods do not intervene directly—Elom is exiled, Tas'va wanders seeking forgiveness, and Rogim is dispersed among mortals. Only the Tasvani and Sentiani remain as active divine presences.

entities.title: Echoes of Derdama
entities.summary: The Echoes of Derdama is an anomalous text found sporadically across libraries, archives, and private collections throughout Avalymia.
entities.contentMd:
The Echoes of Derdama is an anomalous text found sporadically across libraries, archives, and private collections throughout [[Avalymia]]. It is not a stable volume but a shifting entry: a loose page, a marginal note, or an inserted folio that appears where no catalog record claims it should be. The work presents itself as a first-person account delivered by [[Agolel]], the [[Archdemon]] of Forbidden Knowledge.

Whether the voice is truly his, a powerful echo, or a memetic parasite remains debated.

The earliest confirmed appearance of the text comes from [[Derdama]], during the era when scholars sought to map the Black Rivers beneath the continent. The entry’s name derives from the side note originally scrawled in [[Adyni]] ink beside it: “An echo from Derdama, yet not born of this land.”

entities.title: Korr's Apocalypse
entities.summary: The Korr's Apocalypse, known in the oldest Tzanarim echoes as the Shattering of the Standstill, was the cataclysmic event that ended the eternal twilight of the Nirani homeworld.
entities.contentMd:
# Korr's Apocalypse

The **Korr's Apocalypse**, known in the oldest [[Tzanarim]] echoes as the *Shattering of the Standstill*, was the cataclysmic event that ended the eternal twilight of the [[Niran|Nirani]] homeworld. For eons, [[Korr]] had remained fixed in the heavens, one face forever turned toward the blistering gaze of its sun, the other bathed in the sacred, freezing dark.

## The Shattering
The cause of the cataclysm remains a subject of fearful speculation. Some [[Nirani History|histories]] claim a shifting of the [[Universal Resonance Field]] knocked the world from its foundations; others whisper of an ancient, nameless entity that stirred within the planet’s core. Regardless of the source, the result was absolute: Korr began to turn.

## The Creeping Dawn
To the Nirani, who lack the organs of sight and possess skin as fragile as wet parchment under the sun, the rotation was a death sentence. It was not a swift end, but a slow, agonizing crawl. A wall of blistering light and searing wind began to advance across the dark hemisphere, reclaiming the shadows mile by mile. This "Creeping Dawn" boiled the subterranean rivers and scorched the [[Carapace Cities]] to calcified husks.

## The Horrors of the Light Side
As the world turned, the horrors of the eternally sun-baked hemisphere—the *Searing Face*—were dragged into the lands of the dark. These were not merely winds of heat, but ancient and terrible things:
- **Glass-Hided Beasts:** Predators with skins of fused silica that thrived in the solar fire, now hunting the fleeing Nirani in the shifting twilight.
- **Blinding Flora:** Crystalline growths that pulsed with stored radiance, capable of burning the sensitive Nirani through mere proximity.
- **Solar Tempests:** Storms of pure heat and light that roared across the terminator line, scouring the landscape of all moisture.

## The Great Flight
The Apocalypse forced the Nirani into a state of desperate nomadism. They became a people of the flight, forever retreating into the dwindling shadows to escape the sun that sought to consume them. It was this existential dread that ultimately gave birth to the [[First Nirani Expedition]] and, eventually, the [[The Nirani Exodus|Great Exodus]].

entities.title: Nirani Exodus (Narrative)
entities.summary: In ancient times, Korr's Apocalypse caused Korr to shift from its tidally locked state. It began to revolve differently, causing an extremely slow day/night cycle.
entities.contentMd:
In ancient times, [[Korr's Apocalypse]] caused [[Korr]] to shift from its tidally locked state. It began to revolve differently, causing an extremely slow day/night cycle. This event caused a dire climate change, but also forced the [[Niran|Nirani]] to become nomadic, as the dangers of the once-lit side of [[Korr]] became relevant.

The Nirani sought a solution for their exile, and so the [[First Nirani Expedition]] came to be. A group of Nirani explorers was sent on a journey through a magical portal to find a new home for their people.

As they stepped through the portal, the first expedition ended up on the North Pole of [[Ezob]].

The explorers of the first expedition quickly realized that their magic failed as it did not work on Ezob in the same manner it did on Korr. Without their magical abilities, they were unable to communicate with their people on Korr or return through the portal. They were stranded on Ezob.

Upon realizing the First Nirani Expedition had not returned, the elders of Korr became worried and sent out a second expedition to find and rescue the first group. This became known as the [[Second Nirani Expedition]]. The second group also became stranded on Ezob, unable to return to Korr or communicate with their home, and thus the elders of Korr decided to abandon the idea of a new home.

As time passed and the situation on Korr became direr, the Nirani leaders made the difficult decision to organize a mass exodus to Ezob. This became known as [[The Nirani Exodus]]. Thousands of Nirani left their home planet, traveling through the portal to Ezob and establishing a new home on the continent of [[Gavyris]].

The first settlement on Gavyris was named [[Reniran Qarnirai]], and it quickly became the center of Nirani culture on Ezob. The Nirani built a wall to honor and remember their lost home, known as the [[Wall of Korr]]. It depicted the story of the expeditions to Ezob and the Nirani Exodus, serving as a reminder of the sacrifices the Nirani made in their quest for a new home.

To this day, the Nirani continue to thrive on Ezob, while never forgetting the sacrifices of their ancestors and the home they had left behind.

entities.title: Origins of Men (Legend of Earth)
entities.summary: In the annals of Avalymia's history, there exists a legend, whispered through the ages, about a world named Earth—a realm of marvels and wonders.
entities.contentMd:
In the annals of [[Avalymia]]'s history, there exists a legend, whispered through the ages, about a world named [[Earth]]—a realm of marvels and wonders. This myth speaks of Earth as a [[Plane of Existence|plane of existence]] unlike any other in the cosmic tapestry of Avalymia. It was a world where humans, a race of ingenious beings, thrived amidst technological marvels and scientific wonders, far surpassing the knowledge of any known realm.

Earth, it is said, was a vibrant planet teeming with diverse life, grand cities, and vast wildernesses. Humans, adept in harnessing the powers of their world, reached for the stars. They colonized their moon, ventured across their solar system, and sent expeditions into the void of deep space. Their achievements were the pinnacle of their civilization, a testament to their unyielding spirit and boundless curiosity.

But the legends speak of a cataclysmic event, born from the very zenith of human achievement. In their relentless pursuit of knowledge and power, humans unraveled a force they could not control. This force shattered the very fabric of their existence, fracturing Earth into countless world shards, each containing fragments of the planet, celestial bodies, and remnants of human civilization.

These world shards, torn from their origin, were cast adrift in the cosmic sea of Avalymia. Like celestial ships lost in a storm, they wandered, colliding with other planes and realms, scattering humanity across the universe. Each shard carried with it a piece of Earth's legacy, stories of its glory, and echoes of its downfall.

The survivors, finding themselves in strange and alien worlds, clung to the memories of their lost home. Earth became a legend, a mythical paradise from which they were exiled, its memory preserved in tales passed down through generations. It was revered as the ancestral home, a symbol of lost greatness and a beacon of hope for those who dreamed of rediscovering it.

In Avalymia, the myth of Earth resonates with a sense of mystery and adventure. Many believe that the lost world still exists, hidden in the far reaches of the universe, waiting to be found. Adventurers and scholars alike seek the fragments of Earth's history, delving into ancient ruins and deciphering cryptic artifacts, hoping to uncover the truth behind the legend.

Thus, Earth remains a cornerstone of human identity in Avalymia—a lost cradle of civilization, an eternal mystery, and a timeless quest that continues to inspire and haunt the human races and their descendants across the myriad realms of existence.

Established around 6200 BR, this pivotal agreement marked the first formal unification of Nirani society, outlawing interclan warfare and instituting sacred laws regarding the treatment of the dead. Inscribed on intricate slabs of fossilized bone, these laws embodied the collective wisdom and solemn oaths of the clans. The Bone Accord endured as a cornerstone of Nirani society, guiding their civilization through centuries of peace and cultural growth.

entities.summary: The Deathbed is the fourth layer of Derdama, a hellscape composed of organic remains and decay  located beneath the Plains of Desolation.
entities.contentMd:
The Deathbed is the fourth layer of [[Derdama]], a hellscape composed of organic remains and decay  located beneath the [[Plains of Desolation]].

![deathbed](/vaults/avalymia/images/deathbed.webp)

It is a bloody hellscape dominated by rot and decay.

The very ground is made from the remains of creatures and peoples. Mountains of bones and rotting flesh are visible in all directions. Scavengers, vultures, and deadly flesh-eating fungi roam these Deadlands. The [[Bone Cairn]] is a region of the Deathbed in which monsters lurk inside massive skulls and bony remains of ancient beasts.

The Deathbed is a forsaken world which contains many oddities, such as oceans and rivers of blood, massive ash wastes called The [[Ash Lands]].

At the lowest point in this world, in the [[Valley of Souls]], stands a [[Palace of the Unnamed Monarch|palace]]. This palace contains the portal to [[The Scorched Realm]]

entities.title: Palace of the Unnamed Monarch
entities.summary: At the lowest point in the Deathbed lies the Palace of the Unnamed Monarch, a haunting structure shrouded in perpetual gloom and surrounded by rivers of blood and sprawling fields of decay, the palace stands as a bleak…
entities.contentMd:
At the lowest point in the [[Deathbed]] lies the Palace of the Unnamed Monarch, a haunting structure shrouded in perpetual gloom and surrounded by rivers of blood and sprawling fields of decay, the palace stands as a bleak beacon amid the relentless rot. Its towering bone spires pierce the smoky air, while twisted corridors echo with the whispers of lost souls. Within its grand, shadowed halls, a mysterious portal glimmers—a gateway leading to the infernal depths of [[The Scorched Realm]], guarded by the silent, watchful presence of the [[Unnamed Monarch]].

## Whispers of the Ash Lands
> *"The Scavengers of the Ash Lands do not know if the Monarch is a god who forgot his name, or a man who traded it for the right to watch the end of the world."*

entities.title: Derdama
entities.subtitle: Also known as Dermada, Derdamada, Dærdama, Underworld, The Underworld, Hell, The Deep, The Abyss
entities.summary: Derdama, also known as Dermada, Derdamada, Dærdama, and The Underworld, is a world located deep beneath the world of Ezob. It is a dark and treacherous hellscape, often associated with torment and decay.
entities.contentMd:
Derdama, also known as Dermada, Derdamada, Dærdama, and The Underworld, is a world located deep beneath the world of [[Ezob]]. It is a dark and treacherous hellscape, often associated with torment and decay. Derdama is an unearthly and mysterious realm where the laws of nature are commonly ignored.

Derdama is surrounded by myth and legend in most cultures. It is said to host the souls of the damned, and it is believed that death does not exist there. In order to die in Derdama, one's soul must either be destroyed or physically torn apart from their body. As a result, criminals are sometimes sent there to be tormented for eternity.

Ezob is often struck by [[World Shard]]. When this occurs, the area struck by the shard is pushed underneath it and into Derdama, while the shard merges with the world and takes its place.

This process divides the underworld into layers, each with its own characteristics. The upper layers are the most mundane, while the lowest layers are the most ancient and otherworldly.

Although sunlight cannot reach Derdama, some regions of the world are illuminated by other sources of light, such as bioluminescent lifeforms, lava oceans, and a mysterious object called [[The Derdaman Sun]]. However, there are some regions that are illuminated without any apparent source of light at all.

Derdama lies deep beneath the surface of Ezob but reaching it by digging down is practically impossible due to the immense density of the rock layer separating the two.

Derdama has few known entrances, and many more hidden or inaccessible paths all throughout Ezob.

![derdama layers chart](/vaults/avalymia/images/derdama-layers-chart.webp)

entities.title: Graht Mish'ol
entities.subtitle: Also known as The Prison, The Derdaman Sun Prison, The Dungeon of Light
entities.summary: Graht Mish'ol is the name whispered across cultures and ages for a place that may or may not exist at the center of The Derdaman Sun, the lowest layer of Derdama.
entities.contentMd:
Graht Mish'ol is the name whispered across cultures and ages for a place that may or may not exist at the center of [[The Derdaman Sun]], the lowest layer of [[Derdama]]. It is said to be a prison, built by the gods to contain the greatest evil the world has ever known. No one has ever been there. No one has ever returned claiming to have seen it clearly. It exists in the same space as the afterlife, the soul, and divine judgment—believed in deeply, argued about endlessly, and never proven.

The name itself has no traceable origin. It appears in prayers, lullabies, curses, and cautionary tales across civilizations that had no known contact with one another. [[Melidon Flemm]] believed this pointed to a shared primordial source—a fragment of the [[Divine Tongue]] embedded so deeply in mortal memory that it survived the collapse of every language that carried it. [[Lioris Gimmel]], his student, took the idea further: if the name was truly divine in origin, then it was not merely a label but a component of the seal itself—a word that mortals were *meant* to remember, whether they understood why or not.

Neither could explain how cultures separated by oceans and millennia arrived at the same two words.

# The Shape in the Light
Among the very few who have ventured deep enough into the Derdaman Sun and survived, a handful have reported seeing something in the distance—a structure, or the suggestion of one, glimpsed through the blinding radiance. The accounts are vague, contradictory, and often dismissed. Some describe walls. Others describe the absence of walls—a darkness that holds its shape inside the light, like a wound in the brightness. One account speaks of a corridor. Another insists it was a single door, standing alone in an ocean of fire with nothing behind it.

None of these witnesses could say with certainty what they saw. Most recanted or went mad. The few who held to their accounts could never agree on a single detail, except one: whatever it was, it was not natural. It had been placed there. It had been made.

Whether what they saw was Graht Mish'ol, or simply the Derdaman Sun playing tricks on minds never meant to endure its light, remains unknown.

# What Lies Within
Every culture that speaks of Graht Mish'ol agrees on one thing: something is inside. Beyond that, consensus collapses entirely. The nature of the prisoner—if it is a prisoner, if it is singular, if it is even alive—is the subject of myth, not scholarship. There are no texts to cite, no evidence to weigh. There are only stories, passed down through generations, each shaped by the fears and faiths of those who tell them.

What is agreed upon, across nearly every tradition, is that the [[Trinity of Gods]] acted in unison to create Graht Mish'ol. This detail persists even in cultures that disagree on everything else about the gods. In most accounts of divine history, [[Elom]], [[Tas'va]], and [[Rogim]] acted independently or in opposition to one another. Whatever prompted the creation of Graht Mish'ol was apparently severe enough to unite them in a single, deliberate act.

No myth records what that act cost them. But in many tellings, the gods are described as diminished afterward—quieter, more distant, as though something essential had been spent.

# Interpretations
See also: [[The Derdaman Sun]]

The silence surrounding Graht Mish'ol has not prevented belief. If anything, the absence of answers has only deepened the mythology. Among the most widely told interpretations:

- **Orthodox Adonist teaching** holds that the prisoner is a being that predates the [[Trinity of Gods]]—a force so ancient that its very existence was omitted from canonical scripture by divine decree. To speak its name would be to acknowledge it, and to acknowledge it would be to weaken the seal.
- **The Lunar Vigil** teaches that Graht Mish'ol holds the original darkness that existed before the moons rose. The maze of light is not a dungeon but a lantern, and the prison endures only as long as the light burns.
- **The Awakened Cults** are the only known group to speak of the prisoner with longing rather than dread. They believe Graht Mish'ol contains the first being to ever successfully [[Awakened Reincarnation|Awaken]]—a perfected form that the gods imprisoned out of jealousy. Several cult factions have allegedly attempted pilgrimages toward the Derdaman Sun to "liberate" it. None have returned.
- **Nirani oral tradition** does not name the prisoner. The [[Nir|Nirani]] Deep Faith holds that what lies at the center of the Derdaman Sun is not a being but a silence—an anti-resonance, a negation of the [[Universal Resonance Field|Hollow Flame]] itself. They speak of it rarely, and only in metaphor.

> "Every culture pours its deepest fear into that light. The pious see a heretic. The scholars see ignorance. The grieving see something that refused to die. Perhaps that is the true function of Graht Mish'ol—not to imprison what is within, but to reveal what we carry."  
> — [[Lioris Gimmel]], *Meditations on the Unknowable*
