entities.title: The Derdaman Sun
entities.summary: The Derdaman Sun is the lowest layer of Derdama located just beneath the Ghostly Abyss. It is a vast ocean of burning light that houses colossal beasts.
entities.contentMd:
The Derdaman Sun is the lowest layer of [[Derdama]] located just beneath the [[Ghostly Abyss]]. It is a vast ocean of burning light that houses colossal beasts.

This realm contains a maze of light, with a dungeon at its center known as [[Graht Mish'ol]]. According to legends this is where the greatest evil the world had known is imprisoned by the gods.

# The Silence of the Archdemons
Perhaps more unsettling than any legend surrounding the Derdaman Sun is the behavior of the [[Archdemon]]s in its presence. Beings of immense [[Ontological Weight]] who have traversed the deepest and most harrowing layers of [[Derdama]]—entities that have faced oblivion, waged wars across planes, and endured millennia of torment—universally refuse to discuss what lies within the maze of light.

This is not ignorance. The Archdemons are among the oldest and most knowledgeable beings in existence. Nor is it reverence, for they bow to no god and follow no doctrine. It is something else entirely—a silence that feels less like a choice and more like an instinct, as though whatever resides at the center of the Derdaman Sun exists beyond even their capacity to process.

[[Yagon]], who weeps ceaselessly for every suffering soul across the multiverse, falls mute when the subject arises. [[Tynophet]], who fears nothing in her dominion of plague and decay, does not venture near the seventh layer. Even [[Tophet]], whose rage is said to be boundless and indiscriminate, gives the Derdaman Sun a wide and deliberate berth.

No Archdemon has ever explained why. No Archdemon has ever been compelled to. Scholars who have attempted to extract answers through summoning, bargaining, or coercion have reported the same result: the conversation simply ends. The demon does not rage, does not threaten, does not deflect. They merely stop speaking, as though the words themselves refuse to form.

> "I have bound Archdemons in circles of salt and iron. I have heard them howl, bargain, and lie. But when I spoke the words 'Derdaman Sun,' the silence that followed was the first time I ever saw something ancient look afraid."  
> — Attributed to an unnamed demonologist, source unverified

entities.title: Crystal Caverns
entities.summary: Hidden within the ever-shifting tunnels of the Labyrinth, the Crystal Caverns are a breathtaking anomaly in an otherwise grim underworld.
entities.contentMd:
![crystal caverns](/vaults/avalymia/images/crystal-caverns.webp)

Hidden within the ever-shifting tunnels of the [[Labyrinth]], the Crystal Caverns are a breathtaking anomaly in an otherwise grim underworld. These vast subterranean chambers glitter with unearthly splendor — their walls, ceilings, and floors encrusted with towering formations of radiant crystal. Each crystal hums with a faint, melodic resonance, a magical echo said to respond to emotion, memory, or even the passage of souls.

The caverns are not a single location but a network of sacred vaults, each with its own hue and harmony. Some glow with calming blues, others with furious crimson, and a rare few pulse with shifting colors, impossible to name. The deeper one descends, the more bizarre the geometries become — crystals spiraling in impossible directions, forming bridges, arches, and spirals that defy mundane physics.

Though mesmerizing, the Crystal Caverns are fiercely protected. Sentient crystalline lifeforms known as [[Crystarch]] emerge from the walls to defend against intrusion. These beings are semi-transparent, multifaceted creatures that shimmer like living prisms, capable of unleashing focused beams of magic amplified by the ambient crystals.

Some say the caverns themselves are alive, subtly shifting paths to trap intruders, or closing behind those deemed unworthy. Voices echo in impossible directions, and illusions crafted from refracted light may lead travelers in circles for days.

Fragments harvested (rarely and at great risk) from the outermost edges of the caverns are prized by enchanters and arcanists. Known as [[Soulglass]], these shards can store emotion, memory, or even magical energy.

Legends whisper of a secret ritual where a person may fuse their soul into a crystal to become immortal — not as a lich, but as a conscious song within the cavern, joining the eternal harmony of light and sound.

entities.title: Heart of the Labyrinth
entities.summary: At the center of the caverns lies the legendary Heart of the Labyrinth — a colossal, singular crystal the size of a castle spire.
entities.contentMd:
At the center of the [[Crystal Caverns|caverns]] lies the legendary Heart of the Labyrinth — a colossal, singular crystal the size of a castle spire. It pulses with a slow, heartbeat-like rhythm, casting patterns of light across the walls like a dreaming mind. According to ancient lore, the Heart contains an ancient soul — possibly the first soul ever lost in [[Derdama]] — and is believed to hold a forgotten truth or power great enough to reshape the nature of death itself.

Some cults believe it to be a sliver of [[Avalama]]’s sorrow crystallized. Others suspect it is a fractured piece of a [[Foundation Stones|Foundation Stone]], altered by its long slumber beneath the surface.

entities.title: Veil of Still Waters
entities.summary: Tucked into the melancholic vastness of the Plains of Desolation lies the Veil of Still Waters, a realm of eerie quiet and emotional erosion ruled by the Archdemon Anaxa.
entities.contentMd:
![veil of still waters](/vaults/avalymia/images/veil-of-still-waters.webp)

Tucked into the melancholic vastness of the [[Plains of Desolation]] lies the Veil of Still Waters, a realm of eerie quiet and emotional erosion ruled by the [[Archdemon]] [[Anaxa]]. Unlike the searing grief that defines the broader layer, the Veil is a place where sorrow doesn’t scream — it whispers, and then forgets to speak at all. It manifests as a black, motionless sea choked in eternal mist, its surface unbroken save for drifting islands made of memories: fragmented moments, abandoned thoughts, and dreams that lost their will to become real.

Time does not move naturally here. Moments stretch, blur, and fall apart. Travelers who enter the Veil often forget why they came, or even that they came at all. Some lose their names, others lose their will to leave. The waters are not deep in the literal sense, but rather spiritually dense — wading into them is to wade into the self and find it too heavy to lift. At the center of the sea rests Anaxa’s palace: a ruined theater, half-submerged, where echoes of lost applause swirl through the fog.

The Veil serves as a spiritual precursor to the deeper agony found in the Plains. While [[Yagon]] absorbs the suffering of those who have already broken, Anaxa erodes the scaffolding that keeps a soul upright in the first place. Those who fall under her influence begin to let go of their fears, but also their desires, and eventually their sense of self. The Veil doesn’t feed on suffering; it lulls suffering to sleep, smothers it in velvet, and leaves only stillness.

Some believe the Veil is not a punishment but a mercy — a place where pain is silenced rather than sharpened. Others view it as the most insidious prison in all of [[Derdama]]: a sea that drowns not the body, but the reason to swim. Whatever the truth, those who gaze into its black waters too long often find themselves mirrored not as they are, but as they were, just before they stopped trying.

entities.title: The Scorched Realm
entities.summary: The Scorched Realm is the fifth layer of Derdama, a volcanic wasteland dominated by lava and heat located beneath the Deathbed.
entities.contentMd:
![scorched realm view](/vaults/avalymia/images/scorched-realm-view.webp)

The Scorched Realm is the fifth layer of [[Derdama]], a volcanic wasteland dominated by lava and heat located beneath the [[Deathbed]].

entities.title: Silent Abyss
entities.summary: The Silent Abyss (known to the subterranean Nirani as Tal-Vash-Korr, or the "Deep Soundless Void") is a colossal underwater chasm located at the lowest point of the Eladonic Ocean.
entities.contentMd:
The **Silent Abyss** (known to the subterranean [[Niran|Nirani]] as *Tal-Vash-Korr*, or the "Deep Soundless Void") is a colossal underwater chasm located at the lowest point of the [[Eladonic Ocean]]. It acts as a direct planar puncture—a massive tectonic tear that descends into the first layer of the underworld, [[Derdama]].
## The Soundless Maw
The defining physical and magical property of the Silent Abyss is its absolute lack of vibration:
- **Acoustic Dead-Zone:** A permanent silence field blankets the chasm. No sound waves can propagate through its waters; verbal speech, acoustic signals, and sonic spells are instantly flattened and nullified.
- **Endless Waterfall:** Millions of gallons of ocean water pour over the rim of the chasm in a perpetual, titanic undersea waterfall. Because of the planar boundary at the threshold, the water is vaporized or siphoned as it crosses into Derdama, falling silently into the underworld without generating any turbulence.
## Planar Pressure and Madness
Descending into the chasm subjects travelers to extreme [[Abyssal Compression]]:
- **Magical Dampening:** The dense planar boundary dampens spellcasting, causing standard spells to fail and draining the mana reserves of divers.
- **Mental Echoes:** Despite the absolute external silence, survivors of deep-sea expeditions report hearing "internal speech"—whispers echoing directly inside their skulls. Scholars hypothesize that the sensory deprivation of the abyss allows the human mind to tune into the telepathic resonance of ancient cosmic entities slumbering in the rifts of Derdama.

entities.title: Adur
entities.summary: Adur is a province located in southern Meshareen. It is a land of dramatic geography, ancient scholarship, and a unique ecosystem centered around the Silver-Lace Plateaus.
entities.contentMd:
**Adur** is a province located in southern [[Meshareen]]. It is a land of dramatic geography, ancient scholarship, and a unique ecosystem centered around the [[Silver-Lace Plateaus]].

## Geography
The province is characterized by massive limestone mesas separated by deep, mist-filled canyons.
- **[[Silver-Lace Plateaus]]**: The primary geographical feature, home to numerous independent Scholar-Cities.
- **[[The Violet Fields]]**: Vast high-altitude biomes dominated by towering, mana-rich flora.
- **[[Gulf of Adur]]**: The primary maritime boundary to the south.

## Economy & Industry
Adur's economy is inextricably linked to its unique flora and fauna.
- **[[Stone-Silk]]**: A fire-resistant textile harvested from the larvae of the [[Spirescale Moth]].
- **[[Indigo Resin]]**: A versatile fuel and preservative extracted from the [[Violet Spires]].
- **The [[Harvest Flight]]**: An annual event that drives the province's resource collection and cultural life.

## Culture
Adur is a center for [[Orthodox Adonism]] and is home to some of the most prestigious libraries and magical academies in [[Ezob]]. The isolation provided by the plateaus has fostered a culture of deep contemplation and specialized research.

---
**See Also:**
- [[Meshareen]]
- [[Aden]]
- [[Great Pollen-Storm]]

entities.title: Emerald Fields
entities.summary: The Emerald Fields is a sun-bleached, arid coastal region bordering the southern shores of the Gulf of Adur in the province of Adur, on the continent of Meshareen.
entities.contentMd:
The **Emerald Fields** is a sun-bleached, arid coastal region bordering the southern shores of the [[Gulf of Adur]] in the province of [[Adur]], on the continent of [[Meshareen]]. Unlike the lush, violet-dominated highlands of the province, this low-lying basin is defined by dry, reddish clay and massive, jagged crystalline spires of a deep emerald hue that erupt from the parched earth.

## Crystalline Spires and Auroras
The defining feature of the region is the presence of giant green crystals, some rising over thirty meters in height:
- **Petrified Remains:** Scholars from the Adurian libraries believe these crystals are not standard geological formations, but rather the mineralized, petrified biological remains of an ancient, primordial event that occurred before the age of the [[Aden]].
- **Solar Refraction:** During the hot daylight hours, the structures absorb and refract solar light, casting shifting green auroras across the ground.
- **Resonant Hum:** The fields hum with a faint, low-frequency magical vibration. This resonance disrupts compasses and navigation devices, making the area notoriously difficult to map or cross without guides.

## Local Exploitation
Scouts and alchemists brave the arid heat to harvest small crystalline shards. These shards are highly sought after for their magic-refracting properties, used to craft focusing lenses for arcane telescopes and specialized scrying instruments.

entities.title: Gulf of Adur
entities.summary: The Gulf of Adur is the primary maritime body bordering the southern coast of the province of Adur, situated on the continent of Meshareen.
entities.contentMd:
The **Gulf of Adur** is the primary maritime body bordering the southern coast of the province of [[Adur]], situated on the continent of [[Meshareen]]. It serves as a vital shipping channel and a distinct ecological zone, connecting the maritime trade of the southern oceans to the Scholar-Cities of the highlands of [[Ezob]].
## Coastal Geography and Industries
The coastline of the gulf is marked by sheer limestone cliffs, deep sheltered bays, and unique maritime activity:
- **Maritime Shipwrights:** The coastal settlements along the gulf are renowned for building specialized exploration vessels and cargo ships. The local builders utilize timber harvested from the lower valleys, sealed with [[Indigo Resin]] for superior waterproofing.
- **Crystalline Borders:** The western coastline of the gulf borders the arid expanse of the [[Emerald Fields]], where towering green crystalline spires reflect off the shallow waters, creating a shifting green glow known to sailors as the "Emerald Shimmer."
## Oceanic Atmosphere
Due to the unique air currents coming off the [[Silver-Lace Plateaus]], the gulf is prone to sudden, warm fogs. These fogs are often laden with microscopic mana-pollen during the [[Harvest Flight]], creating glowing nighttime sea-mist that can either guide sailors or induce vivid, magical hallucinations in crews who fail to wear protective veils.

entities.title: Silver-Lace Plateaus
entities.summary: The Silver-Lace Plateaus are a dramatic geographical feature located in the province of Adur on the continent of Meshareen.
entities.contentMd:
The **Silver-Lace Plateaus** are a dramatic geographical feature located in the province of [[Adur]] on the continent of [[Meshareen]]. This region is defined by its massive limestone mesas that rise abruptly above deep, mist-filled canyons, creating a "shattered" landscape of extreme elevations.
## Geography and Climate
The plateaus are named for the intricate, lace-like patterns of silver-grey limestone visible on their sheer cliff faces. The environment is characterized by:
- **Alkaline Soil:** The soil is highly chalky and alkaline, a remnant of ancient seabed deposits. This prevents the growth of traditional forests but supports a specialized ecosystem of drought-resistant, giant shrubbery and the dominant **[[Violet Spires]]**.
- **The Luminous Mist:** The canyons between the mesas are perpetually filled with a thick, white mist that reflects the periwinkle light of the sky, often making the plateaus appear as if they are floating upon a sea of clouds.
- **Periwinkle Skies:** Due to the constant release of mana-pollen from the flora, the sky over the plateaus never reaches true darkness, maintaining a permanent twilight hue.
## Ecosystem: The Violet Fields
The summits of the plateaus are home to **[[The Violet Fields]]**, a unique biome dominated by 15-meter-tall lavender-like stalks. This ecosystem supports the massive **[[Spirescale Moth]]** and various other specialized fauna adapted to high mana concentrations.
## Cultural Importance
The Silver-Lace Plateaus are considered the "Intellectual Heartland" of the [[Aden]] people. The relative isolation of each mesa has led to the development of independent **Scholar-Cities**, connected only by aerial travel (via moths or airships) and intricate bridge-works.

entities.title: The Violet Fields
entities.summary: The Violet Fields (also colloquially known as the Lavender Fields) is a vast, high-altitude biome situated atop the Silver-Lace Plateaus in Adur.
entities.contentMd:
**The Violet Fields** (also colloquially known as the **Lavender Fields**) is a vast, high-altitude biome situated atop the [[Silver-Lace Plateaus]] in [[Adur]]. It is widely regarded as one of the most visually stunning and magically active regions in [[Meshareen]].
## Atmosphere
The fields are defined by a permanent "Mana-Haze." As the **[[Violet Spires]]** release their indigo pollen, the air becomes saturated with a fine, glowing dust. This creates a dream-like quality where distances are difficult to judge, and the light is filtered into soft shades of violet and periwinkle. The air carries a constant, sharp scent of camphor and honey, a result of the **[[Indigo Resin]]** produced by the towering stalks.
## Ecosystem
The biome is characterized by:
- **Flora:** Dominated by the **[[Violet Spires]]**, which grow in dense, uniform "forests" across the plateau tops.
- **Fauna:** 
    - The primary inhabitant is the **[[Spirescale Moth]]**, whose white forms are often seen gliding above the purple canopy. 
    - The parasitic **[[Pollen-Flea]]**, which clings to the moths and drains their mana.
    - The **[[House Wyrm]]**, which hunts the fleas in mid-air.
- **Soil:** The chalky, white limestone soil provides a stark contrast to the deep purple of the plants, though it is often obscured by a layer of fallen indigo pollen.
## Human Activity
The local [[Aden]] population has built their society around the rhythms of the fields. 
- **Resin Harvesting:** A dangerous but lucrative occupation involving the collection of the thick sap from the blooms.
- **Silk Cultivation:** The harvesting of **[[Stone-Silk]]** from the caves beneath the fields.
- **The [[Harvest Flight]]:** An annual event where the relationship between the moths and the harvesters is celebrated and utilized for mass collection of resources.
## Phenomena
The fields are the site of the **[[Great Pollen-Storm]]**, a seasonal occurrence that is both a natural wonder and a significant magical hazard.

- **[[Limparho]]**: A neighboring continent to the east, separated by the [[Erillian Ocean]].

## Notable Features
- **[[Silver-Lace Plateaus]]**: A unique geological formation in the south.
- **[[Indigo Resin]]**: One of the continent's most prized exports.

entities.title: Ru'una (Moon)
entities.summary: Ru'una is the primary moon of Ezob. While it holds profound religious significance as a divine guardian, it is also a site of immense biological and astronomical interest.
entities.contentMd:
Ru'una is the primary moon of **[[Ezob]]**. While it holds profound religious significance as a divine guardian, it is also a site of immense biological and astronomical interest.

![ruuna](/vaults/avalymia/images/ruuna.webp)

# Appearance and Observation
From the surface of Ezob, Ru'una does not appear as a barren, grey satellite. Instead, it glows with a vibrant, emerald-green hue.

When viewed through high-precision lenses or arcane telescopes, the moon reveals a world teeming with activity:
- **Verdant Expanses:** Large portions of the lunar surface are covered in what appear to be massive, undulating forests or fungal mats of deep jade and lime.
- **Signs of Life:** Long-range observations have confirmed the existence of **primitive lifeforms**. These appear to be massive, slow-moving mega-fauna and complex flora that pulse in rhythm with Ezob's own magical tides.
- **Atmospheric Veil:** The moon is shrouded in a thin, shimmering atmosphere that refracts light into brilliant auroras, contributing to its protective reputation.

# Cultural and Religious Significance
Ru'una is regarded as a living deity in many religions, most notably within [[The Lunar Vigil]].
- **The Divine Lantern:** It is believed that [[Elom]] crafted Ru'una to serve as a watchtower against the darkness of [[Derdama]]. Its vibrant green light is often interpreted as "active life" standing in defiance of the entropic rot of the underworld.
- **The Vigil Cycle:** The phases of Ru'una dictate the safety of the Ezobian nights. The Full Moon (The Vigil) is a time of maximum protection, while the New Moon (The Blind Days) is feared as a time of celestial vulnerability.

# Baselyle
**Baselyle** is a fortified town situated at the mouth of the [[Grizyle River]] on the rocky cliffs of [[Edis Detria]] in the [[Spine of the East]]. As one of the primary ports of call on the "Broken Island," the town acts as a vital trade hub for the eastern archipelago. The settlement is defined by its stone sea-walls and a bustling harbor market that serves passing merchant ships.

The town's market has become the primary destination for the crops grown by the exiled Miozin family. The sought-after [[Miozin Cherries]], [[Miozin Brandy]], and [[Miozin Jam]] are brought to Baselyle's harbor docks by the trader [[Tarek ya Harek]], who sells them to local residents and visiting crews.

entities.title: Miozin Manor
entities.summary: Miozin Manor is a secluded estate located in a mist-shrouded volcanic valley within the island of Edis Detria, a fractured land in the Spine of the East archipelago.
entities.contentMd:
# Miozin Manor
**Miozin Manor** is a secluded estate located in a mist-shrouded volcanic valley within the island of [[Edis Detria]], a fractured land in the [[Spine of the East]] archipelago. Constructed primarily of dark, weathered pine timber harvested from the island's interior forests, the manor serves as the sanctuary and home of the [[Zovik Miozin|Miozin family]], who were banished from the nearby town of [[Baselyle]] after Zovik adopted the [[Niran|Nirani]] orphan [[Kheresh]]. Today, the estate is famous among travelers for its sprawling orchard of [[Miozin Cherry Tree|Miozin Cherry Trees]].

## The Timber Estate
The estate consists of several timber-framed structures built to withstand the damp, ash-heavy air of the valley:
- **The Manor House:** A two-story residence constructed from heavy, pitch-coated pine logs, featuring wide hearths and low ceilings designed to trap heat.
- **The Drying Barns:** Large, well-ventilated wooden sheds where the harvested cherries are spread across mesh trays to dry or cure.
- **The Root Cellar:** A deep stone-and-timber vault dug into the cold northern hillside, used to preserve fresh fruit and store preserves.
- **The Cooperage and Tool Shed:** A smaller workshop where Zovik drafts crates and repairs agricultural tools.

## The Outcast's Orchard and Trade
Following their banishment, the Miozin family cleared a wild, ash-clogged basin on the southern slopes of Edis Detria's central ridge. The volcanic soil, combined with cold mineral runoff from the island's high plateaus, proved exceptionally fertile for fruit cultivation. The orchard is comprised of dozens of gnarled [[Miozin Cherry Tree|Miozin Cherry Trees]] that bloom with pale, ghost-white blossoms in the early spring, bearing [[Miozin Cherries]] by late summer.

Because the Miozin family is forbidden from entering Baselyle, they cannot sell their produce themselves. Instead, they rely on [[Tarek ya Harek]], a merchant who travels to the manor to purchase the harvest. Tarek sells the cherries, Vesna's specialized [[Miozin Brandy]], and her rich [[Miozin Jam]] at a premium stall in Baselyle's harbor market. Although the townsfolk refuse to permit the family's return, the popularity of the fruit among passing travelers and captains has made the trade highly lucrative for both the Miozins and their proxy.

entities.title: Dudai
entities.summary: Dudai is a sprawling, bustling trade city located on the northern coast of the Inner Sea of Yarin.
entities.contentMd:
Dudai is a sprawling, bustling trade city located on the northern coast of the [[Inner Sea of Yarin]]. Known colloquially as the "Gateway of Ash and Gold," it is a massive mercantile hub where legitimate maritime commerce collides with the dangerous, subterranean smuggling of underworld relics.
# Geography and The Maw
Dudai is built around a wide natural harbor that accommodates ships from across the Inner Sea and the [[Eladonic Ocean]]. However, its most defining and dangerous feature lies just outside the city's eastern walls: **The Sunken Gate** (often simply called "The Maw"). 

This massive, spiraling chasm descends deep into the crust of [[Ezob]], serving as a rare, direct physical passage into the upper layers of [[Derdama]] (specifically, The [[Labyrinth]]). Because of this proximity, the air in the city's eastern districts often carries a faint, unsettling scent of sulfur and ozone mixed with the salty sea breeze.

![dudai](/vaults/avalymia/images/dudai.webp)

# Economy and The Markets
The city's economy is entirely driven by trade, divided roughly into two spheres:
* **The Sunlit Piers (The Grand Bazaar):** The legitimate, above-board markets where serious merchants deal in bulk. Here, one can find [[Dwarf|Dwarven]] metallurgy, mundane textiles, grain, and raw materials shipped across [[Yarin]]. It is loud, vibrant, and heavily regulated.
* **The Ash Markets (The Undermarket):** A chaotic, winding bazaar of shadowy stalls where the true, dangerous wealth of Dudai flows. Dubious merchants peddle counterfeit magical items and snake-oil cures, while seasoned scavengers sell genuine, highly illegal finds dragged up from Derdama. Items like raw [[Soulglass]], abyssal flora like [[Dreamcap (Resource)|Dreamcaps]], and demon-tainted relics are haggled over in hushed tones.
# Governance: The Iron Ledger
Dudai is ruled not by a king or mayor, but by a powerful Merchant Guild known as **[[The Iron Ledger]]**. Comprised of wealthy Dwarven merchant-princes and human oligarchs, the Guild cares nothing for morality—only for commerce, order, and the sanctity of contracts. 

They maintain a ruthless private mercenary force to keep the peace and enforce trade laws. Most importantly, The Iron Ledger tightly controls, heavily guards, and taxes access to The Maw. They ensure they take a cut of every Derdaman relic brought to the surface, willingly turning a blind eye to the occasional demonic corruption such trade invites into the city, so long as the taxes are paid.

entities.title: The Sunken Gate
entities.summary: The Sunken Gate, commonly known as The Maw, is a colossal, spiraling chasm located just beyond the eastern walls of the city of Dudai.
entities.contentMd:
# The Sunken Gate (The Maw)
The Sunken Gate, commonly known as **The Maw**, is a colossal, spiraling chasm located just beyond the eastern walls of the city of [[Dudai]]. It is one of the few known points on [[Ezob]] where the physical boundary between the surface world and the upper layers of [[Derdama]] is naturally and permanently breached.
# Geography and Descent
The Maw appears as a jagged, circular sinkhole nearly half a mile in diameter. Its walls are lined with ancient, weathered stone and a winding, precarious path—partially natural and partially carved by centuries of use—that spirals down into the darkness. 

As one descends, the temperature drops and the air becomes heavy with the "Abyssal Scent": a mixture of cold stone, sulfur, and the faint, metallic tang of the [[Nexus|Nexus']] influence. The bottom of the spiral opens directly into the higher reaches of The [[Labyrinth]], the first layer of Derdama.

![the sunken gate the maw](/vaults/avalymia/images/the-sunken-gate-the-maw.webp)

# Control and Taxation
Because of its immense strategic and economic value, The Maw is strictly controlled by [[The Iron Ledger]]. 
* **The Gatehouse:** A massive, fortified bridge and checkpoint spans the narrowest part of the chasm, where the Merchant Guild's mercenaries (The Scale-Guards) monitor all traffic.
* **The Toll:** Every individual entering or leaving The Maw must pay a steep "Descent Tax." Furthermore, [[The Iron Ledger]] claims a 20% "Relic Tithe" on any artifacts brought up from the depths.
# Dangers
Beyond the physical risk of the descent, The Maw is a source of constant "Planar Seepage." The proximity to Derdama causes localized temporal distortions and a higher-than-average incidence of [[Demonic Corruption (Condition)]] in the nearby districts of Dudai. The Merchant Guild employs specialized "Censer-Bearers" to burn sacred resins along the rim of the chasm to dampen these effects, though their efficacy is often questioned.

[[Scavenger|Delvers]] who brave the descent often report hearing whispers from the depths long before they reach the bottom—a phenomenon known as "The Caller's Wind."

entities.title: Bel-Vakkiath
entities.subtitle: Also known as Domain of Frost-Stone
entities.summary: Bel-Vakkiath (Nirani: The Domain of Frost-Stone) is the vast, artificially frozen region of the Great Desert of Yarin that surrounds the city of Belraz.
entities.contentMd:
**Bel-Vakkiath** (Nirani: *The Domain of Frost-Stone*) is the vast, artificially frozen region of the **[[Great Desert of Yarin]]** that surrounds the city of **[[Belraz]]**. It is defined by the radius of effect of the **[[Frozen Heart of Belraz]]**, extending many kilometers from the city center.

## Geography and Environment
Bel-Vakkiath is a monochrome landscape of silver, grey, and bone-white. The environment is characterized by [[Frost-Silt]], a unique substance formed when desert sand is flash-frozen and permeated by the supernatural chill of the Frozen Heart.

* **The Silt-Crust:** The surface is often a hard, brittle crust of frozen mica and sand. Beneath this layer lies "Fluid-Frost," a semi-liquid silt that can be plowed or burrowed through by specialized creatures.
* **Mica Blizzards:** Intense winds whip up mica dust and ice crystals, creating blinding storms that can shred exposed flesh.
* **Frost-Fumaroles:** Geothermic vents from the desert floor that erupt through the ice, creating localized "Mist-Oases" where bioluminescent **[[Bel'sha]]** (Frost-Bloom) grows.

## Flora and Fauna
The region is home to lifeforms that have either been imported by the [[Niran|Nirani]] or have evolved to exploit the artificial winter.
* **[[Nirdaxtalakh]] (Mole-Ox):** The primary draft animal, found in the wilder fringes and domestic "Wool-Fiefs."
* **[[Qarzirtalakh]] (Frost-Grain):** Vast terraces of this tuber are cultivated in the inner circles of the expanse.
* **Ice-Borers:** Subterranean arthropods that feed on the thermal variations near the Frost-Fumaroles.

## Settlements and Outposts
While Belraz is the heart of the region, the Expanse is dotted with smaller hubs of activity:
* **[[Wool-Fiefs]] (Nir’bel-Qarn):** Agricultural hamlets dedicated to Nirdaxtalakh herding and wool production.
* **The Rim-Markets:** Trading posts on the very edge of the frost-zone where [[Ash-Nomads]] and other desert dwellers exchange goods with the Nirani.

## Peculiarities
* **The Glass Forests:** Large areas where sand has been fused into jagged, crystalline structures that amplify the low-frequency hums of the earth.
* **Thermal Mirage:** Near the edges of Bel-Vakkiath, the collision of extreme heat and extreme cold creates "False-Vents"—visual distortions that lure travelers into lethal mica-pits.

---
*See also: [[Belraz]], [[Frozen Heart of Belraz]], [[Nirdaxtalakh]], [[Great Desert of Yarin]]*

entities.title: Belraz
entities.summary: Belraz (Nirani: Hidden Secret) is a major Nirani city located in the heart of the Great Desert of Yarin.
entities.contentMd:
# Belraz

**Belraz** (Nirani: *Hidden Secret*) is a major [[Niran|Nirani]] city located in the heart of the [[Great Desert of Yarin]]. Unlike the subterranean metropolis of [[Reniran Qarnirai]], Belraz is an above-ground bastion of ice and bone-white stone, surviving the desert’s scorching heat through the power of the [[Frozen Heart of Belraz]].

## History
Founded roughly two centuries after the [[Nirani Exodus (Narrative)|Nirani Exodus]], Belraz was established following the discovery of a massive thermodynamic anomaly in the central desert. Nirani explorers from [[Gavyris]] identified a "void-pulse" where the desert’s heat was being consumed by a buried Foundation Stone. Seeing this as a divine reclamation of their home-plane, **[[Korr]]**, high-ranking [[Whiteskin]] and [[Greyskin]] houses funded a deliberate colonization. 

The city was built in concentric rings around the central Temple of the Heart, protected by the **Vortashuran** (The Breath-Wall)—a permanent, towering mist of freezing fog created by the temperature clash between the city and the desert.

## Architecture and Adaptation
Living above ground requires extreme architectural and biological discipline.
* **Bel’vakk (Frost-Masonry):** Buildings are constructed from a dense composite of desert sand and mineral-rich condensation, flash-frozen into permanent, windowless structures. These walls are several feet thick to provide thermal insulation.
* **Vash’nir (Breath-Eyes):** Instead of windows, homes feature narrow, spiraling acoustic vents that catch the whistling desert winds, translating them into a "song" that the eyeless inhabitants use to tell the time and the intensity of the sun.
* **Ulamirrvakk (Memory-Stone):** The exterior walls are engraved with deep, tactile reliefs—providing both historical narrative and navigation markers for the Nirani’s sensitive fingertips.

## The Zir’kashūran (Sun-Veils)
To survive the sun's glare, the people of Belraz wear **Zir’kashūran**. These multi-layered garments are woven from **Nir’wool** (harvested from the **[[Nirdaxtalakh]]**) or **Zir’flax** (locally cultivated sand-flax). All exposed cloth is treated with **Dax’lur**, a reflective tallow made from rendered beast-blubber and mica dust, giving the citizens a shimmering, silvery appearance.

## Agriculture and Economy
Belraz is a capitalistic meritocracy driven by above-ground agriculture within the **Zim’khoratal** (Frost-Fields).
* **Qarzirtalākh (Sand-Starch):** The primary crop. A hardy, tuberous root used to bake **Bel’qar** (Frost-Bread).
* **Zir’valaraz (Glimmer-Flour):** The city's primary export. Prized by [[The Iron Ledger]], this flour never spoils and provides a strange, focused energy. Its secret ingredient is **Ash-Remnant** fertilizer, which induces a heat-resistant docility and physical dependency in consumers.
* **[[Nirdaxtalakh]] (Blind-Ox):** Massive, mole-like mammals that serve as the city's primary livestock, providing meat, marrow (**Dax’bel**), and wool.

## The Secret and the Shard
The "Secret" of Belraz is protected by the lethal environment of the **Vortashuran**, which kills uninvited intruders through "Flash-Crystallization" of the lungs. For those who must leave the city, **Ulabelraz** (Heart-Shards) are carried as amulets. These fragments of the Foundation Stone create a localized "Cold-Sleeve," protecting the traveler from the desert sun for several days.

***
**See Also:**
* [[Frozen Heart of Belraz]]
* [[Nirdaxtalakh]]
* [[Qarzirtalakh]]
* [[The Iron Ledger]]

entities.summary: The Obsidian Grotto is a hidden subterranean sanctuary deep beneath Korr’s surface, renowned among the ancient Nirani clans for its gleaming black walls carved from volcanic glass.
entities.contentMd:
![obsidian grotto](/vaults/avalymia/images/obsidian-grotto.webp)

The Obsidian Grotto is a hidden subterranean sanctuary deep beneath [[Korr]]’s surface, renowned among the ancient [[Niran|Nirani]] clans for its gleaming black walls carved from volcanic glass. Legend speaks of the cavern forming through volcanic upheaval, leaving behind smooth, reflective obsidian surfaces that shimmer dimly under the bioluminescent glow of subterranean fungi. Historically, the Grotto served as neutral ground where the twelve Great Nirani Clans convened to establish the [[Bone Accord]], the foundational treaty governing peace among their peoples. Echoes linger mysteriously in the glassy chamber, preserving whispers from long-past ceremonies, giving rise to the belief that the obsidian walls retain memory itself. Now regarded as sacred, the Obsidian Grotto remains a pilgrimage site, where descendants of the Nirani journey to reflect upon their history or seek clarity in the timeless depths of its reflective darkness.

entities.title: Agolel
entities.summary: Agolel, Archdemon of Knowledge, Secrets, and Madness, also known as The Whisperer in the Dark, The Eye of the Abyss, Lords of Secrets and The Keeper of the Unseen, is a being of great power and terror that has shaped…
entities.contentMd:
![agolel 2](/vaults/avalymia/images/agolel-2.webp)

Agolel, Archdemon of Knowledge, Secrets, and Madness, also known as The Whisperer in the Dark, The Eye of the Abyss, Lords of Secrets and The Keeper of the Unseen, is a being of great power and terror that has shaped the very fabric of existence with his insidious machinations.

Agolel's appearance is a grotesque sight to behold, he is a twisted abomination of flesh, covered in a miasma of tentacles and writhing appendages that writhe and pulsate with an unearthly energy. His many eyes, each a window to the abyss, peer out from behind writhing tendrils of blackness. His stench is overwhelming, a mixture of decaying flesh and sulfur that makes mortals gag and retch in his presence.

His voice is a harsh whisper that sounds like a thousand souls screaming in agony. He speaks in riddles and cryptic phrases, revealing only as much knowledge as he deems necessary to his followers. His realm resides in the [[Labyrinth]] of [[Derdama]]. It is a labyrinthine library of forbidden tomes, filled with dark secrets and ancient wisdom that only the bravest or most foolish dare to seek.

Agolel's cult, known as the [[Brotherhood of The Black Tome]], is a shadowy organization that has been secretly influencing the world for centuries. They worship their dark master as a god, offering up sacrifices and performing unspeakable rituals in his name. They believe that the knowledge he possesses holds the key to unlocking the secrets of the universe, and that by serving him, they will gain the power to reshape reality to their will.

![agolel 1](/vaults/avalymia/images/agolel-1.webp)

Agolel's artifacts are feared and coveted by mortals, for they hold immense power and can be used to achieve great feats. The champions of Agolel are often given these artifacts as gifts, using them to spread their master's influence across the mortal realm. Agolel The most famous of these artifacts is the [[Tome of Forbidden Knowledge]] also known as The Black Tome, a massive tome bound in human flesh and inked in blood.

Another artifact is [[Agolel's Eye]] also known as Orb of Secrets, The Vessel of Forbidden Visions, a crystal ball that can reveal hidden knowledge and visions of the future.

Finally, there is the [[Blade of Agony]], also known as The Severer of Realities, a long, wickedly sharp sword, made of a twisted, black metal that seems to absorb light. It is said that Agolel used the Blade to carve his own realm out of the underworld, and that its power can be harnessed by mortals who dare to wield it.

entities.title: Anaxa
entities.summary: Anaxa, The Siren of Sadness, The Mistress of Melancholy, The Queen of Apathy, The Lady of Longing, The Forgotten Flame, is the Archdemon of Depression, Apathy, Lust, and Hollow Desire.
entities.contentMd:
>"Come now. Rest. The world has asked too much of you already. Lay your burdens beside mine, and forget what it felt like to care."

![anaxa](/vaults/avalymia/images/anaxa.webp)

Anaxa, The Siren of Sadness, The Mistress of Melancholy, The Queen of Apathy, The Lady of Longing, The Forgotten Flame, is the Archdemon of Depression, Apathy, Lust, and Hollow Desire. Once a radiant muse of mortal longing, Anaxa fell from grace when her divine hunger for beauty became an addiction to adoration. In her descent, the vibrant flame of her purpose guttered into smoldering ash, leaving behind a twisted soul caught between yearning and numbness.

Now, she embodies the ache of desire without fulfillment, the weariness of motion without meaning. Her influence is insidious, not through violence or conquest, but through slow unraveling. She is the whisper in the ear when the bed feels too heavy, the cold breath behind the kiss that means nothing, the smile that hides the rot.

Anaxa appears as a paradox of allure and decay. Her form shifts between seductive grace and grotesque collapse. Her skin bears the sheen of fading glamour, stretched thin over bones that seem both fragile and unyielding. Her hair, once lustrous, is now tangled with threads of ash and withered petals. Her eyes shimmer with longing, yet are hollow with absence.

Her voice is low and melodic, like a lullaby sung through tears, and her presence is accompanied by the scent of wilted roses and spent perfume.

![anaxa 2](/vaults/avalymia/images/anaxa-2.webp)

Anaxa's domain is The [[Veil of Still Waters]] a vast, stagnant sea shrouded in mist. Black waters reflect the stars but distort every reflection. Here, time slows to a crawl. Islands of faded memories and broken dreams drift slowly across the surface. Souls who enter often forget why they came. Some become statues of salt, others sink beneath the waves, singing wordless songs of what could have been.

At the center lies her palace: a ruined theater submerged halfway into the sea, echoing with applause from an audience long gone.

[[The Vesper Repose]] is a secretive, elegiac sect that venerates Anaxa as the goddess of quiet surrender. They do not seek to conquer, but to lull. Their rites involve narcotic incense, whispered confessions, and rituals of slow undressing—both literal and spiritual. They preach that true power lies in detachment, and that peace is found not in action, but in beautiful stillness.

Some within the cult believe Anaxa can be healed, that deep within her indolence is a hidden ember still burning. Others believe the world must decay into her image to reach perfect tranquility.

![anaxa 3](/vaults/avalymia/images/anaxa-3.webp)

# Artifacts
**The [[Lacuna Veil]]** - A gossamer shroud that, when worn, numbs all sensation. It allows the bearer to resist pain, but also joy. The longer it is worn, the more one forgets their purpose.
**The [[Mirror of Yearning]]** - A hand-held mirror that shows not what is, but what the viewer most craves. Staring into it too long induces apathy, as the real world pales beside illusion.
**[[Kiss of Ash]]** - A small vial of silvery powder that, when inhaled or applied, induces blissful euphoria followed by deep melancholia. Addictive in both body and soul.
# Narrative Role
Anaxa is a force of corrosion rather than conflict. She doesn’t destroy with fire but with forgetfulness. In stories, she works best as a looming temptation or a tragic caution. Her most effective role is as a mirror: forcing protagonists to confront their own emptiness, their need for validation, or the fear of meaninglessness.

Yet, there is potential for redemption. Hidden deep beneath her lassitude is a fractured will that once wanted to _inspire_. Whether she can be reignited or is destined to fade is a question the world may never answer.

entities.contentMd:
In the depths of the underworld, where the souls of the damned writhe in eternal agony, there lurks the Archdemon Timtometh, also known as Mistress of Illusion, the Deceiver of Souls, the Harbinger of Ignorance, and the Manipulator of Truth.

![timtometh](/vaults/avalymia/images/timtometh.webp)

Her form is grotesque and twisted, an abomination to behold, with limbs that seem to twist and writhe unnaturally, and a repulsive stench emanating from her every pore. Her voice is a rasping whisper that sends shivers down the spines of even the most hardened of demons.

Timtometh rules over the realm of the [[Ghostly Abyss]], a place where illusions reign supreme, and the truth is a scarce commodity. Her realm is shrouded in a dense fog, and the very air seems to shimmer with an otherworldly light, which obscures the true nature of everything within it. Timtometh's interests lie in the manipulation of knowledge and the propagation of ignorance, for she knows that with the right illusions and deceptions, she can control the minds of mortals and demons alike.

There are those who worship Timtometh as a goddess, drawn to her power and the promise of knowledge and truth. Her cultists are known as the Veiled Ones, and they work tirelessly to spread her influence in the mortal realm. They wear masks that obscure their features and weave intricate illusions to deceive those who would oppose their mistress.

Timtometh has created powerful artifacts that aid in her agenda of spreading ignorance and illusion. The first of these is the [[Veil of Shadows]], a cloak that imbues its wearer with the ability to move undetected in darkness and cast illusions that obscure their presence. The second is the [[Mirror of Lies]], a mirror that reflects not the truth but the illusions that its wielder wishes to show. Those who gaze into it see not what is, but what Timtometh wishes them to see.

The third and most powerful of Timtometh's artifacts is the [[Staff of Deception]], a staff that grants its wielder the power to weave intricate illusions that can bend the very fabric of reality itself. Those who fall under the staff's sway find themselves lost in a web of lies and illusions, unable to distinguish reality from falsehood.

entities.title: Tophet
entities.summary: In the depths of the underworld, where the tormented souls of mortals suffer in agony for eternity, there resides Tophet, the Archdemon of fire, destruction, genocide, and chaos.
entities.contentMd:
![tophet](/vaults/avalymia/images/tophet.webp)

In the depths of the [[Derdama|underworld]], where the tormented souls of mortals suffer in agony for eternity, there resides Tophet, the [[Archdemon]] of fire, destruction, genocide, and chaos. Tophet, also known as the Lord of Flames, the Bringer of Destruction, and the Harbinger of Chaos, is a being of immense power and malevolence. His mere presence is enough to bring about the end of worlds, and those who cross his path do so at their own peril.

Tophet's appearance is extremely repulsive, his body twisted and malformed to the point of being otherworldly. His skin is a deep, crimson red, and his eyes are a blazing inferno, radiating with an intense malevolence that would strike fear into the hearts of even the bravest of warriors. His horns are twisted and sharp, capable of rending even the strongest armor with ease. His clawed hands drip with venom, and his wings are charred black, like the remnants of a long-forgotten fire. His entire being exudes a putrid stench that chokes the very air around him.

Tophet's realm, [[The Scorched Realm]] is a barren wasteland where the ground is scorched, and the skies are choked with smoke and ash. The realm reflects the demon's own desires, a place where destruction, death, and suffering are the only constants.

His followers, a cult known as the [[Children of the Inferno]], are a fanatical bunch, who worship Tophet as a god. They see him as a purifier, who seeks to rid the world of the weak and the impure. They perform horrific rituals in his name, sacrificing innocents to appease their dark master.

Tophet has created several powerful artifacts over the years, each imbued with a fraction of his own power. The most feared of these is the [[Blade of Ash]], a sword forged from the blackest obsidian and infused with the power of fire. The blade burns with searing heat, capable of melting even the strongest of metals. Those who are struck by the Blade of Ash are consumed by flames, their bodies reduced to nothing but ash in a matter of moments.

Another artifact created by Tophet is the [[Scepter of Cataclysm]]. The Scepter is a twisted and gnarled staff, carved from the bones of long-dead demons and adorned with jewels that flicker with an eerie red light. When wielded by Tophet or one of his chosen minions, the Scepter can summon forth waves of infernal flames that scorch everything in their path. The Scepter can also open portals to other dimensions, allowing demons and other malevolent beings to pour forth into the mortal world, spreading destruction and chaos in their wake. Those who are caught in the path of the Scepter's power are incinerated or dragged screaming into the Abyss.

entities.title: Tynophet
entities.summary: Tynophet, the Archdemon of Filth, Decay, Plagues, and Diseases, known as the Filthmonger, Lady of Decay, the Rotten Queen, Mother of Pestilence, is an ancient Archdemon of unparalleled darkness.
entities.contentMd:
Tynophet, the Archdemon of Filth, Decay, Plagues, and Diseases, known as the Filthmonger, Lady of Decay, the Rotten Queen, Mother of Pestilence, is an ancient Archdemon of unparalleled darkness.

![tynophet](/vaults/avalymia/images/tynophet.webp)

She is a sight to behold. Her twisted, gnarled form stands tall and imposing, a hulking mass of decay and filth. Her sickly gray skin is mottled with patches of decaying flesh, covered in festering sores and weeping wounds.

A putrid aroma wafted from her being, surrounding her, a noxious cloud of death and decay, mixed with the buzzing of flies and the sound of coughing that echoes through the caverns of [[Mephitia]].

Her long, tangled hair is infested with lice and dandruff which wriggle and crawl as she moves. Her eyes are dark and glazed, pulsing with black veins. Her teeth are blackened and rotten, and her tongue is coated in a thick layer of slime that seemed to constantly drip from her lips. Every breath she takes is a struggle, each wheeze and cough sounding like the last gasp of a dying creature, echoing with the gurgling of mucus in her lungs.

As she moves, swarms of insects and vermin scuttle around her, drawn to the decay and filth that she embodies. Her touch brings death and decay, causing living beings to rot and wither away. She has the power to create plagues and diseases that can wipe out entire civilizations, and she revels in the destruction and suffering that her powers bring.

Tynophet is a creature of immense power, an ancient demon lord with her own realm within the underworld - Mephitia, a land of mossy caverns, mushroom forests, and mires filled with boiling tar.

She is revered as a goddess by a cult known as [[The Plaguebearers]], who worship her as the bringer of disease and decay. The Plaguebearers are a group of mortals who had devoted themselves to Tynophet's cause, and they would willingly spread her plagues and diseases among the living, hoping to gain her favor.

Tynophet had created many powerful artifacts and weapons over the centuries, each with its own unique power. One of her most infamous creations was The [[Plague Rat]], a rat-shaped figurine that, when placed near a body of water, would cause the water to become contaminated with a lethal disease.

Another artifact created by Tynophet was [[Corpse Crown]], a macabre headdress made from the skulls and bones of the dead. The crown has the power to raise the dead and turn them into mindless zombies.

[[Swarm Caller]] is a twisted device that can summon and control swarms of Khin. it appears as a small, intricately designed box made of bone and metal, covered in intricate runes and sigils that glow with a sickly light, indicating the presence of demonic energy. When activated, the Swarm Caller emits a low, buzzing hum, and a cloud of dark, winged insects pour out of the box.

entities.title: Yagon
entities.summary: Yagon, Archdemon of Grief and Loss, is known across Avalymia as the Wailing Lord, the Mourning Shade, and the Whispering Sorrow.
entities.contentMd:
Yagon, Archdemon of Grief and Loss, is known across Avalymia as the Wailing Lord, the Mourning Shade, and the Whispering Sorrow. Unlike most entities born of darkness, Yagon neither delights in nor actively seeks suffering. Instead, he is eternally haunted by it—cursed with a near-omniscient awareness of every heartbreak, betrayal, and loss experienced throughout the multiverse. His existence is an endless cycle of empathetic torment, turning him into a tragic yet dangerous figure, feared not for malice but for the contagious despair that emanates from him.

Yagon possesses two forms, reflecting the duality of grief:
# Manifest Form
Tall and slender, cloaked in layers of tattered silks and veils that flow as if underwater. His flesh is porcelain pale, marked with fine cracks from which silvery mist escapes. His eyes resemble galaxies of sorrow—dark voids flickering with the light of endless suffering. This form evokes quiet dread and mournful beauty, allowing Yagon to interact with the world without overwhelming it.

![yagon manifest form](/vaults/avalymia/images/yagon-manifest-form.webp)

# True Form
Revealed only in moments of overwhelming sorrow or rage, Yagon's true form is grotesque and monstrous—a twisted mass of jagged bone, seeping sores, and ancient scars. His eyes become pitch black and empty, his breath reeks of rot and sulfur, and his footsteps leave puddles of tears. This form is both a weapon and a curse, embodying grief so viscerally that it corrodes the minds of those who witness it.

The cracks of his Manifest Form act as a fragile seal, barely containing the full force of his torment. When pushed too far, his beauty fractures, revealing glimpses of the horror beneath.

As she wept beside the altar, the silver mist grew thick. Then, for the briefest moment, his eyes hollowed into black voids, and a jagged rib cracked through the silk.  

>“I’m sorry,” Yagon whispered, re-shrouding himself. “Sometimes, the sorrow slips through.”

>“The form he shows reflects your stage of grief. Mourners see the veiled prince. The broken see the corpse.”

>“He wears beauty like a funeral shroud, hiding the true rot beneath.”

![yagon true form](/vaults/avalymia/images/yagon-true-form.webp)

Yagon resides in the Plains of Desolation, a domain mirroring his internal anguish. Instead of simply barren wastes, his realm is a melancholic tapestry of silent ruins and abandoned cities, eternally suspended in twilight. Monuments crumble slowly, forgotten gardens wither quietly, and whispering breezes carry echoes of lost laughter and distant mourning. Souls lost in this plane often wander, trapped in their most painful memories, unable to find closure or release.

Yagon's greatest desire is liberation from his ceaseless pain. He actively seeks an end to his torment but remains uncertain whether that lies in oblivion or redemption. His actions often revolve around attempts to alleviate suffering—occasionally manifesting as warped acts of mercy, pulling grieving souls into his realm to shelter them from harsher fates. Yet each act of compassion deepens his sorrow, for every soul’s pain becomes his own, perpetuating his internal struggle between empathy and self-preservation.

Yagon maintains complex interactions with beings across Avalymia. His worshippers, the Children of Grief, revere him with misguided devotion, mistaking his torment for divine wisdom. He treats them with gentle melancholy, often advising them in cryptic parables, trying to subtly guide them away from their destructive worship.

Among the other Archdemons, he is viewed with suspicion and pity, for they sense the genuine sorrow beneath his power. Yagon occasionally engages with mortals and immortals who seek insight into the nature of suffering, offering truths that both enlighten and devastate. Each interaction further weaves him into the larger narrative of Avalymia, influencing events in subtle, profound ways.

# Artifacts
**[[Tear of Despair]]**: A luminous gem born from Yagon’s own essence, encapsulating pure sorrow. Instead of merely inducing grief, it provides the bearer profound empathy, revealing the hidden sorrows of others. It is a powerful, transformative object that can either heal or destroy, depending on the wielder's strength of character.
**[[Mirror of Regret]]**: A reflective artifact that allows observers to confront their deepest regrets in vivid clarity. Yagon uses it sparingly, often to test mortals or to force them into self-reflection, ultimately aiming for catharsis or growth rather than mere suffering.

# Narrative Role
In Avalymia’s stories, Yagon serves as both an antagonist and tragic guide—a character whose interactions force protagonists and readers alike to confront the raw, unfiltered reality of grief. Through him, narratives explore the importance of healing, acceptance, and the strength found in vulnerability. Yagon is not merely a force of sadness, but a complex figure whose existence challenges others to grow beyond their suffering, even if he himself cannot.

![yagon residence](/vaults/avalymia/images/yagon-residence.webp)

entities.title: Beast of The Red Forest
entities.summary: The Beast of the Red Forest is a creature of legend, feared and revered by the Cusaru who inhabit Istandir.
entities.contentMd:
The Beast of the Red Forest is a creature of legend, feared and revered by the [[Cusaru]] who inhabit [[Istandir]]. It is said to be a massive creature, constructed of debris such as driftwood and rocks that have been animated by a [[Foundation Stones|Foundation Stone]] at its core. The Beast is thought to be a powerful and ancient entity, with great strength and resilience.

The Beast is said to roam [[The Red Forest]], searching for prey and attacking anything that it perceives as a threat. It is believed to be nearly invulnerable, with thick layers of debris protecting its Foundation Stone core. The Beast is also said to possess great magical powers, which it can use to intimidate its victims.

The Beast of the Red Forest is shrouded in mystery and legend, and little is known about its true nature or purpose. Some believe that it is a manifestation of the forest's own power and magic. Whatever its origins, the Beast is a formidable and awe-inspiring presence in the Red Forest, and one that commands respect and fear from all who encounter it.

entities.contentMd: The Starlight Seekers are a race of highly advanced humanoid robots made of golden metal and turquoise glass. They have visible moving parts in their glass head and are equipped with advanced artificial intelligence. Their mission is to explore and colonize new planes, and they can adapt to new environments and repair themselves. They help the local species of the planets they settle by sharing their knowledge and technologies and working with them to find solutions to problems. They can multiply by building more of their own kind with resources gathered on their travels.

entities.title: Avalymian Moth
entities.summary: The Avalymian Moth is a majestic and mythical creature of immense size, often described as a living embodiment of the Avalymian Cloud itself.
entities.contentMd:
The Avalymian Moth is a majestic and mythical creature of immense size, often described as a living embodiment of the [[Avalymian Cloud]] itself. With a wingspan that can stretch several meters, it is a sight to behold, its iridescent wings shimmering with a myriad of colors that reflect the magical energy of the universe.

Its body is covered in a soft, luminescent fur that glows with an ethereal light, casting a soft, comforting glow in the darkness of the Avalymian Cloud. Its eyes, large and round, are said to hold a depth of wisdom and knowledge beyond mortal comprehension, capable of seeing through the veils of reality to perceive all the planes of existence.

The Avalymian Moth's most remarkable ability is its power to travel through the Avalymian Cloud and between different planes of existence. It achieves this through a unique form of magic inherent to its species, allowing it to fold space and time around its massive form. When it takes flight, it leaves behind a trail of sparkling, magical dust, which is said to have powerful alchemical properties.

Despite its size and power, the Avalymian Moth is a gentle and peaceful creature. It is often associated with guidance and transition, seen as a guide for lost souls or a herald of significant change. Legends tell of the moth appearing to individuals who are about to undergo a significant transformation or journey, its presence a sign of the shifts to come.

The Avalymian Moth is a rare sight, its appearances often becoming the stuff of legends and tales passed down through generations. To witness an Avalymian Moth in flight is considered a blessing, a once-in-a-lifetime spectacle of natural and magical wonder.

entities.title: Doomnix
entities.summary: The Doomnix is a flightless, heavily built species of domesticable avian livestock native to the polar wastes of Gavyris and Amarah, but raised extensively in the volcanic archipelagos of the southern Spine of the East.
entities.contentMd:
The **Doomnix** is a flightless, heavily built species of domesticable avian livestock native to the polar wastes of [[Gavyris]] and [[Amarah]], but raised extensively in the volcanic archipelagos of the southern [[Spine of the East]].

![doomnix](/vaults/avalymia/images/doomnix.webp)

## Morphology and Volcanic Adaptations
The Doomnix has evolved to survive in highly volatile, high-temperature environments:
- **Flightless Stature:** They have long, highly muscular legs, dense bones, and vestigial wings. While unable to fly, their elongated legs allow them to sprint at high speeds across rugged basalt terrain.
- **Ash-Grey Plumage:** Their feathers are naturally fireproof, absorbing volcanic soot and minerals. This creates a dusty, smoldering appearance that blends in with volcanic ash fields.
- **Ignitable Flank Wires:** Extending from their lower flanks are twelve stiff, wire-like feather shafts. During the mating season, the male coats these bare shafts with flammable, sulfur-rich oils secreted from their uropygial gland. By striking them against volcanic basalt rocks, they ignite the wires into brilliant, smoldering orange trails of flame to impress females in courtship displays.
- **Mineral & Sluggish Diet:** Doomnix feed on volcanic ash, sulfur-rich soil, raw mineral ores, and high-temperature fauna such as [[Magma Slug|magma slugs]]. Their highly specialized, acidic digestive systems break down these highly corrosive materials, producing unique metabolic byproducts.

## Agricultural and Commercial Utility
The Doomnix is considered a prized livestock animal among volcanic communities:
- **[[Doomnix Feathers]]:** Their thick plumage is harvested during molting, used to weave flame-retardant [[Doomnix Garments]].
- **[[Doomnix Meat]]:** A dark, nutrient-dense meat that retains thermal energy long after cooking, protecting consumers from extreme polar cold.
- **[[Doomnix Egg]]:** Obsidian-hard eggs that must be incubated in active lava vents to hatch.
- **Refining Flux:** Their mineral-dense droppings are collected by metalworkers and used as a potent flux to purify ore during smelting.

entities.title: Armavorn
entities.summary: The Armavorn, revered in Niran lore as the primordial architects of subterranean sanctuaries, were colossal Draconian beasts that roamed the depths of ancient Korr.
entities.contentMd:
The Armavorn, revered in [[Niran]] lore as the primordial architects of subterranean sanctuaries, were colossal [[Dragon|Draconian]] beasts that roamed the depths of ancient [[Korr]]. Their massive, stone-like carapaces, intricately layered with scales and rugged ridges, provided inspiration for the early Nirani when constructing their underground shelters, which came to be known as [[Carapace Cities|Carapace City]].

Adapted impeccably for subterranean life, the Armavorn possessed powerful limbs terminating in immense, sharp digging claws, enabling them to carve extensive tunnels and chambers within the planet's crust. Their heavily armored, elongated heads, entirely eyeless due to their existence in eternal darkness, were capable of perceiving their surroundings through vibrations and subtle shifts within the earth.

Despite their formidable appearance and immense strength, the Armavorn were predominantly docile creatures, subsisting mainly on subterranean fungi and minerals. Encounters between the Armavorn and ancient Nirani were marked by mutual respect, with Nirani regarding these creatures as sacred guardians of the underworld. It was considered a significant omen and blessing if an Armavorn chose to rest near a burgeoning Carapace City, believed to bestow protection and good fortune upon the settlement.

Today, while the Armavorn are believed to have vanished following the catastrophic events leading to Korr's Apocalypse, their memory lives vividly within Nirani culture, immortalized in the architecture of their settlements and the intricate carvings decorating the revered [[Wall of Korr]].

![armavorn](/vaults/avalymia/images/armavorn.webp)

entities.title: Calcified Bone Drake
entities.summary: The Calcified Bone Drake is a specialized, wingless species of Drake that has uniquely adapted to the morbid environment of the Deathbed, the fourth layer of Derdama.
entities.contentMd:
The **Calcified Bone Drake** is a specialized, wingless species of [[Drake]] that has uniquely adapted to the morbid environment of the [[Deathbed]], the fourth layer of [[Derdama]]. They are widely regarded as the apex scavengers of the Deadlands, perfectly camouflaged among the mountains of remains that define the layer.
## Appearance
The most striking feature of the Calcified Bone Drake is its "armor," which is not composed of traditional scales but of a thick, jagged layer of calcified biological matter. 
*   **Camouflage:** Its hide is a mottled grey and bone-white, making it virtually invisible when standing still among the ruins of the [[Bone Cairn]].
*   **Skeletal Aesthetics:** Its head is narrow and skull-like, with deeply recessed, glowing red eyes that can pierce the thick ash of the [[Ash Lands]]. 
*   **Physicality:** It possesses four powerful, clawed limbs designed for climbing over unstable piles of bone and tearing through the toughened hides of other Derdaman entities.
## Ecology and Behavior
Unlike the more aggressive dragons of the surface worlds, the Bone Drake is a patient ambush predator. It will often remain motionless for days, appearing as nothing more than a particularly large pile of ribs or a weathered skull, waiting for scavengers or unfortunate travelers to wander within striking distance.

*   **Diet:** It primarily feeds on the marrow of ancient beasts and the residual spiritual essence found within the decaying remains of the Deathbed.
*   **Breath Attack:** Instead of fire, the Bone Drake exhales a "Necrotic Ash"—a cloud of fine, calcified dust that rapidly drains the vitality of living creatures and causes a premature "softening" of their physical form (a precursor to [[Demonic Corruption]]).
## The Palace Sentinel
Rumors persist among [[Scavenger|Scavengers]] that a particularly massive and ancient Calcified Bone Drake, known as the **Cairn-King**, guards the approach to the [[Palace of the Unnamed Monarch]] in the [[Valley of Souls]]. It is said that its scales are composed of the fossilized bones of failed heroes and that its roar carries the whispers of the thousands it has consumed.

entities.title: Dune Wyrm
entities.summary: The Dune Wyrm is a species of sand-burrowing creatures that inhabit the shifting sand-seas of the Great Desert of Yarin on the continent of Yarin.
entities.contentMd:
The **Dune Wyrm** is a species of sand-burrowing creatures that inhabit the shifting sand-seas of the [[Great Desert of Yarin]] on the continent of [[Yarin]]. Sharing a lightly serpentine, draconic morphology, they are relatively modest in scale, typically reaching a size comparable to a desert camel or pack beast (about 3 to 5 meters in length). Unlike highly spiky or dragonesque beasts, the Dune Wyrm is closer to a sand worm in appearance, possessing a smoother, milder silhouette without sharp, aggressive pointiness.

![dune wyrm](/vaults/avalymia/images/dune-wyrm.webp)

## Morphology and Subterranean Movement
Dune Wyrms are uniquely adapted to survive the intense friction and heat of the desert sands:
- **Segmented Carapace:** Their long, cylindrical, worm-like bodies are encased in heavy, overlapping plates of silica-fused bone. These plates are smooth and rounded, matching the curvature of their bodies to minimize friction while burrowing, rather than forming sharp, jagged scales.
- **Seismic Navigation:** Entirely blind, Dune Wyrms navigate and hunt by sensing subterranean vibrations through their armored skin, detecting the movements of nearby caravans or wildlife from several hundred yards away. Their heads are simple and worm-like, lacking eyes or prominent draconic horns.
- **Glass-Melting Maw:** To tunnel through packed sandstone and gravel, their maws secrete a highly acidic, superheated enzyme. This substance melts sand into liquid glass, which cools into smooth, hollow crawlways.
## Ecological Impact
The behavior of Dune Wyrms shapes the local environment of Yarin:
- **Dune Shifting:** Their burrowing causes minor, localized sand-slides and shifts the desert surface, occasionally covering tracks.
- **Harvesting Paths:** Nomadic clans and [[Niran|Nirani]] miners occasionally explore the narrow, glass-lined crawlways left by Dune Wyrms to navigate the desert beneath the blistering sun.
- **The Primordial King:** While standard Dune Wyrms are camel-sized hunters, the oldest and largest individual of this lineage is the legendary, colossal [[Serpent King]], worshiped by the [[Sand Witches]].

entities.title: House Wyrm
entities.summary: The House Wyrm is a finger-sized, parasitic member of the Dragon family prevalent throughout southern Meshareen.
entities.contentMd:
![house wyrm](/vaults/avalymia/images/house-wyrm.webp)

The **House Wyrm** is a finger-sized, parasitic member of the [[Dragon]] family prevalent throughout southern [[Meshareen]]. Though technically a [[Wyrm]], it is widely considered a public health hazard and a persistent nuisance rather than a majestic creature.
## Appearance and Behavior
House Wyrms are exceptionally fast, capable of outmaneuvering common flies and even magical projectiles. They possess slender, iridescent bodies and no limbs, moving through the air with a high-frequency undulating motion. This flight produces a distinctive, high-pitched "whirring" or "drilling" sound, similar to a mosquito but significantly louder, which can become deafening when they swarm.

In the wild areas of [[Adur]], they are the primary predators of the **[[Pollen-Flea]]**. Using their immense speed, they pluck the parasitic beetles directly off the bellies of flying [[Spirescale Moth]]s, serving as a natural control on the flea population.

## The Adurian Summer
These creatures are most active during the Adurian Summer, drawn to the humid mist and the magically-charged atmosphere of the urban settlements. They function as "Mana-Vampires," using a bone-tipped proboscis to feed on the biological energy of sapient beings. 

A bite from a House Wyrm results in a "Numb-Sting"—a magical reaction that leaves a glowing, itchy welt. To combat them, residents of [[Adur]] often employ "Static-Lanterns" or burn incense to disrupt the wyrms' senses.

entities.title: Serpent King
entities.summary: The Serpent King (known as Sarkor-Vath in the ancient dialects of the desert nomads) is a unique, legendary sand-leviathan that slumbers deep beneath the Great Desert of Yarin on the continent of Yarin.
entities.contentMd:
# Sarkor-Vath, the Serpent King
The **Serpent King** (known as *Sarkor-Vath* in the ancient dialects of the desert nomads) is a unique, legendary sand-leviathan that slumbers deep beneath the [[Great Desert of Yarin]] on the continent of [[Yarin]]. While standard [[Dune Wyrm|Dune Wyrms]] are camel-sized creatures of modest scale, Sarkor-Vath is a titanic colossus of mythic proportions, stretching hundreds of cubits through the dark earth.

## The Slumbering Leviathan
The scale of the Serpent King is gargantuan, and its presence is felt across the shifting sand-seas:
- **Vitrified Carapace:** Over hundreds of years, the intense heat and crushing pressure of the deep desert have vitrified its skin, leaving its massive segmented body protected by spiky plates of glass-hard obsidian and fused silica.
- **Earth-Shaking Tremors:** The subterranean movements of the Serpent King are so powerful that they trigger desert quakes, collapse wells, and cause massive dune-slides above.
- **Deep Dormancy:** The leviathan spends centuries in a deep sleep, its breathing generating a heavy, low-frequency throb—the "Dune-Hum"—that ripples through the rock layers of Yarin.

## Competing Legends of Origin
Scholars and cultists have long debated how a creature sharing the lineage of the modest Dune Wyrm could reach such terrifying proportions:
- **The Earth-Hum Stone Hypothesis:** A controversial theory among certain [[Niran|Nirani]] scholars suggests that Sarkor-Vath nested adjacent to a buried, hypothesized [[Earth-Hum Stone]] eons ago. They theorize that the stone's localized temporal distortion slowed the passage of time in the nesting cavern, allowing the wyrm to experience subjective millions of years of uninterrupted biological growth while only centuries passed on the surface.
- **The Progenitor Myth:** The [[Sand Witches]] reject scholarly speculation, worshiping Sarkor-Vath as a primordial deity of soil and stone. In their faith, the sleeper is not a mutant wyrm, but the mother-father of the desert who predates the lesser Dune Wyrms entirely.
- **The Relic of the Contraction:** A cosmological myth suggests the leviathan is a physical crystallization of [[Avalama]]'s sorrow, shaped during [[El Adoniah Detalash Roni]] (the Contraction of the universe) and left to slumber in the deep dark before time began.

## The Hum-Cult and the Dread of Awakening
The Serpent King remains a focal point of dread and worship:
- **The Witches' Pact:** The Sand Witches guard the subterranean shrines surrounding the sleeper's nest. They draw their sand-weaving rituals directly from the rhythmic vibrations of the titan's breathing.
- **The Dread of Awakening:** It is feared by nomads and scholars alike that the Serpent King's slow, rhythmic breathing is what holds the shifting sands of Yarin in place. Should the leviathan ever fully awaken, its violent movements could collapse the desert floor, swallowing the oasis-cities of Yarin into the hollows beneath the earth.
